items.q: Among these implant metals, which has the elastic modulus closest to that of cortical bone?
items.e: Ti-6Al-4V has a modulus of about 110 GPa, against roughly 200 GPa for stainless steel, 210-230 GPa for cobalt-chromium and about 185 GPa for solid tantalum; cortical bone is about 15-20 GPa, so titanium causes the least stress shielding of these.

items.q: Which surface treatment of a cementless titanium implant most actively promotes bone ongrowth?
items.e: Hydroxyapatite is osteoconductive and bonds directly to bone; polished, silicone or PMMA surfaces do not encourage bone ongrowth.

items.q: Wolff's law states that bone remodelling depends mainly on:
o: The magnitude and direction of the mechanical stress it carries
items.e: Bone adds mass and aligns its trabeculae along lines of stress, and loses mass where it is unloaded.

items.q: A 70-year-old woman with stage 4 chronic kidney disease receives her first injection of denosumab 60 mg for osteoporosis. Ten days later she has perioral tingling and carpopedal spasm. The most likely cause is:
items.e: Denosumab suppresses osteoclastic resorption abruptly; patients with advanced CKD or vitamin D deficiency are at highest risk of symptomatic hypocalcaemia, so calcium and vitamin D should be corrected first.

items.q: According to the ASBMR task force, after how many years of oral bisphosphonate (alendronate) should a drug holiday be considered in a woman who is no longer at high fracture risk?
items.e: Reassess after 5 years of oral (3 years of IV zoledronate) therapy; low-risk patients can take a drug holiday, which reduces the small risk of atypical femoral fractures.

items.q: A 66-year-old woman develops multiple new vertebral fractures nine months after stopping denosumab, which she had taken for four years. The mechanism is:
o: Rebound surge in osteoclast-mediated bone resorption
items.e: Stopping denosumab causes a rebound overshoot in bone turnover with rapid loss of bone density; a bisphosphonate should be started when denosumab is stopped.

items.q: In suspected pyogenic vertebral osteomyelitis with negative blood cultures, the best investigation to identify the organism is:
o: CT-guided percutaneous biopsy of the disc and vertebral body
items.e: Image-guided biopsy for culture and histology identifies the organism (and excludes tuberculosis) so that targeted antibiotics can be given; MRI shows the extent, not the organism.

items.q: An immunocompromised man has severe back pain and paraplegia that has been progressing for 12 hours. MRI shows a rim-enhancing epidural abscess from T8 to T10 compressing the cord. The most appropriate management is:
o: Oral antibiotics and repeat MRI in a week
Emergency surgical decompression and drainage with IV antibiotics
items.e: A progressing neurological deficit from a spinal epidural abscess needs urgent decompression together with antibiotics; antibiotics alone are reserved for patients without deficit or unfit for surgery.

items.q: A 28-year-old footballer has an isolated injury of the anterolateral ligament (ALL) of the knee on MRI. The ACL is intact and there is no rotatory instability. Management is:
o: ALL reconstruction combined with ACL reconstruction
Arthroscopic debridement followed by delayed ALL reconstruction
items.e: ALL reconstruction is considered as an addition to ACL reconstruction in selected high-risk patients; an isolated ALL injury with an intact ACL is managed non-operatively.

items.q: The standard screening test for exogenous testosterone use in sport is:
items.e: A urinary T/E ratio above 4:1 is suspicious and is confirmed by isotope-ratio mass spectrometry, which distinguishes synthetic from natural testosterone.

items.q: A 25-year-old with recurrent anterior shoulder dislocation has an off-track (engaging) Hill-Sachs lesion and glenoid bone loss of about 10%. The most appropriate arthroscopic procedure is:
items.e: With subcritical glenoid bone loss, an off-track Hill-Sachs lesion is filled by remplissage (tenodesis of the infraspinatus and posterior capsule into the defect) added to the Bankart repair; McLaughlin is for reverse Hill-Sachs lesions in posterior dislocation.

items.q: A newborn after a difficult delivery holds the arm adducted and internally rotated, with the elbow extended and forearm pronated (waiter's tip), and cannot abduct the shoulder or flex the elbow. The level of injury is:
items.e: Erb-Duchenne palsy affects C5-C6 (upper trunk), paralysing the deltoid, external rotators, biceps and supinator; C8-T1 injury (Klumpke) affects the hand.

items.q: Three weeks after a brachial plexus injury, which finding indicates neurapraxia rather than axonotmesis?
o: Normal nerve conduction distal to the lesion with no fibrillation potentials
items.e: Neurapraxia is a conduction block without axonal loss, so there is no Wallerian degeneration: distal conduction stays normal and denervation potentials do not appear. Paralysis occurs in both; an advancing Tinel sign shows regenerating axons after axonotmesis.

items.q: A 28-year-old woman has an 8 cm, painless, enlarging mass deep to the fascia in the posterior thigh. MRI shows a heterogeneous, enhancing lesion. The most appropriate next step is:
o: Core-needle biopsy along the planned incision line, with staging
items.e: A deep mass over 5 cm is a sarcoma until proved otherwise; a core biopsy placed so that its tract can be excised with the tumour gives the diagnosis and grade, and chest CT completes staging before definitive surgery.

items.q: Three years after resection of a thigh leiomyosarcoma with clear margins, a solitary 2 cm lung nodule is found and no other disease. Which statement is correct?
o: Pulmonary metastasectomy can improve survival in selected patients
Surgery is contraindicated for sarcoma metastases
Whole-lung radiotherapy is the standard treatment
items.e: Complete resection of limited lung metastases in soft-tissue sarcoma, with a controlled primary and a long disease-free interval, offers prolonged survival in selected patients.

items.q: Loss of nuclear expression of which marker on immunohistochemistry supports a diagnosis of malignant peripheral nerve sheath tumour (MPNST)?
items.e: Many MPNSTs, especially high-grade and radiation-associated ones, lose H3K27me3 because of PRC2 inactivation; desmin and myogenin are muscle markers and MDM2 amplification marks well-differentiated and dedifferentiated liposarcoma.

items.q: If the object-to-image distance is kept constant, reducing the source-to-image distance (SID) on a radiograph will:
items.e: Magnification equals SID divided by source-to-object distance; bringing the tube closer increases geometric magnification, which is why a standard long SID is used for templating.

items.q: On CT, increasing the tube voltage from 120 kV to 140 kV with the tube current (mAs) unchanged will:
o: Reduce image noise and patient dose
items.e: Dose rises roughly with the square of the kV at constant mAs: (140/120) squared is about 1.36. Noise falls, but dose rises.

items.q: The inverse square law states that radiation intensity:
o: Falls in proportion to the square of the distance from the source
Falls in proportion to the distance from the source
Doubles when the kV is doubled
items.e: Doubling the distance from the source reduces the intensity to a quarter, which is why stepping back from the C-arm greatly reduces the surgeon's exposure.

items.q: Which metabolic change is most implicated in the pathogenesis of corticosteroid-induced osteonecrosis of the femoral head?
o: Hyperlipidaemia with fat emboli and marrow fat-cell enlargement
items.e: Steroids raise serum lipids, enlarge marrow fat cells and cause fat emboli, raising intraosseous pressure and reducing blood flow to the femoral head.

items.q: A 34-year-old has a displaced intra-articular distal radius fracture with a 3 mm articular step-off and dorsal tilt persisting after closed reduction. The most appropriate treatment is:
o: Open reduction and volar locking plate fixation
Bridging external fixator without reduction of the articular surface
items.e: In a young, active patient, an articular step-off of more than 2 mm after reduction predicts post-traumatic arthritis; open reduction and stable internal fixation restore the joint surface and allow early movement.

items.q: When planning lumbar fusion to avoid postoperative sagittal imbalance, the commonly used alignment target is:
o: Pelvic incidence minus lumbar lordosis (PI-LL) less than 10 degrees
Lumbar lordosis greater than 60 degrees in every patient
items.e: Lordosis should be matched to the patient's pelvic incidence: a PI-LL mismatch of more than 10 degrees, pelvic tilt over 20 degrees and SVA over 5 cm are associated with disability (SRS-Schwab).

items.q: In an asymptomatic adult, the C7 plumb line falls 3 cm anterior to the posterosuperior corner of S1. This indicates:
items.e: A sagittal vertical axis of up to 5 cm is considered normal; more than 5 cm indicates positive sagittal imbalance.

items.q: Which of the following is a major criterion for periprosthetic joint infection in the 2018 ICM definition?
o: A sinus tract communicating with the joint or prosthesis
items.e: The major criteria are a sinus tract communicating with the joint, or two positive cultures of the same organism; CRP, alpha-defensin and a single positive culture count only as minor criteria in the scoring system.

items.q: A 23-year-old footballer has a complete radial tear of the posterior root of the medial meniscus, with no arthritis. The most appropriate treatment is:
o: Transtibial pull-out repair of the root
items.e: A root tear abolishes hoop stresses, behaving like a total meniscectomy; anatomical root repair (commonly transtibial pull-out) restores function in young patients without arthritis.

items.q: A rugby player has episodes of knee locking after a collision. Plain radiographs are normal. The best investigation to look for a chondral loose body is:
items.e: Purely cartilaginous loose bodies and the donor defect are invisible on radiographs; MRI shows the fragment, the defect and associated meniscal or ligament injury.

items.q: All of the following are true of fresh osteochondral allograft transplantation in the femoral condyle EXCEPT:
o: Size matching of donor to recipient condyle is important
The graft does not need to incorporate biologically
It can be combined with meniscal procedures
items.e: The allograft bone must still be incorporated by creeping substitution; only the cartilage survives as viable donor tissue.

items.q: A 2-year-old has a completely absent thumb (Blauth type V) with a normal index finger. The reconstruction of choice is:
items.e: Index pollicization, ideally around 1-2 years of age, is the standard for Blauth IIIB, IV and V; toe-to-thumb transfer is mainly used for traumatic or transverse absence.

items.q: The investigation of choice for a suspected osteochondral lesion of the first metatarsophalangeal joint in a runner with normal radiographs is:
items.e: MRI shows cartilage, subchondral oedema and lesion stability; CT shows bony detail but not cartilage.

items.q: The characteristic microscopic feature of normal hyaline articular cartilage is:
o: Chondrocytes in lacunae within a matrix of type II collagen and proteoglycan
items.e: Articular cartilage is avascular and aneural; its chondrocytes sit in lacunae in a type II collagen and aggrecan matrix.

items.q: Intra-articular corticosteroid injection is absolutely contraindicated in:
o: Gouty arthritis after infection is excluded
items.e: Steroid in an infected joint suppresses local defences and accelerates cartilage destruction; infection must be excluded before any intra-articular steroid.

items.q: Which best explains how mechanical overload leads to osteoarthritis of articular cartilage?
o: Chondrocytes reduce proteoglycan synthesis and increase metalloproteinase activity
items.e: Abnormal loading drives catabolic chondrocyte activity: proteoglycan loss, MMP and aggrecanase (ADAMTS) activity, and collagen network breakdown.

items.q: Which cytokine is a key mediator of synovial inflammation and cartilage proteoglycan breakdown?
items.e: TNF-alpha (with IL-1) induces MMPs and aggrecanases; IL-4, TGF-beta and TIMP-1 are anti-inflammatory or protective.

items.q: A 3-year-old has bowed legs, widened wrists and cupping and fraying of the metaphyses. Serum 25-hydroxyvitamin D is low, calcium is low-normal, and ALP and PTH are high. First-line treatment is:
items.e: This is nutritional rickets; vitamin D with adequate calcium heals it, and most bowing corrects without surgery.

items.q: In vitamin D-deficiency rickets, which finding is NOT expected?
items.e: Low calcium absorption causes secondary hyperparathyroidism, so PTH is high; PTH-driven phosphaturia lowers phosphate, and ALP rises.

items.q: A 28-year-old woman has diffuse bone pain. Calcium is normal, phosphate is low and alkaline phosphatase is high. Bone biopsy shows wide unmineralised osteoid seams. The diagnosis is:
items.e: Wide osteoid seams mean defective mineralisation (osteomalacia). Hypophosphatasia has a low ALP, and primary hyperparathyroidism has high calcium.

items.q: Which test best reflects the body's vitamin D stores?
items.e: 25(OH)D has a long half-life and reflects stores; 1,25(OH)2D is tightly regulated by PTH and may be normal or even high in deficiency.

items.q: The characteristic radiological finding of osteomalacia in an adult is:
o: Cupping and fraying of the metaphyses
items.e: Looser zones are bilateral, symmetrical lucent bands perpendicular to the cortex, typically in the pubic rami, femoral neck and scapula; metaphyseal cupping and fraying occur only in children with open physes (rickets).

items.q: The earliest and most reliable clinical sign of acute compartment syndrome of the forearm in an alert patient is:
o: Pain on passive stretch of the involved muscles
items.e: Pain out of proportion and pain on passive stretch appear early; pulselessness, pallor and complete sensory loss are late signs, after muscle damage has begun.

items.q: A 27-year-old manual worker has tingling in the ring and little fingers with weak interossei. Sensation over the dorsum of the ulnar hand is normal, and nerve conduction shows a block at the wrist. The site of compression is:
o: Proximal forearm between the FCU heads
items.e: Sparing of the dorsal cutaneous branch, which leaves the ulnar nerve proximal to the wrist, localises the lesion to Guyon's canal.

items.q: A 35-year-old woman has numbness of the palmar thumb, index and middle fingers with weakness of abductor pollicis brevis. The nerve involved is:
items.e: The median nerve supplies sensation to the radial three and a half digits on the palmar side and innervates APB through its recurrent motor branch.

items.q: The most widely used test to confirm carpal tunnel syndrome is:
items.e: Nerve conduction shows prolonged distal median latency and slowed sensory conduction across the wrist; ultrasound (cross-sectional area) is a useful adjunct.

items.q: Which of the following is NOT a cause of post-traumatic ankle arthritis after a tibial pilon fracture?
o: Chondral damage to the talar dome at injury
Cartilage loss at the talonavicular joint
Residual articular step-off of the tibial plafond
Malunion with malalignment of the distal tibia
items.e: Post-traumatic ankle arthritis follows tibiotalar articular damage, residual incongruity or malalignment; the talonavicular joint is not part of the ankle joint.

items.q: A 12-year-old has a permeative lesion of the femoral diaphysis. Biopsy shows small round blue cells with strong membranous CD99 and nuclear FLI1 positivity; desmin and myogenin are negative. The diagnosis is:
items.e: Membranous CD99 with FLI1 (reflecting the EWSR1-FLI1 fusion) is typical of Ewing sarcoma; desmin and myogenin negativity excludes rhabdomyosarcoma. Lymphoblastic lymphoma can also be CD99 positive, so molecular confirmation is advised.

items.q: The characteristic chromosomal translocation in Ewing sarcoma is:
items.e: About 85% of Ewing sarcomas carry t(11;22) fusing EWSR1 with FLI1. t(X;18) marks synovial sarcoma and t(12;16) myxoid liposarcoma.

items.q: Module 1: Memory-Based Previous Year MCQs, High-Yield Concepts & Analytical Explanations Section A: Total Hip Arthroplasty (THA) Biomechanics & Surgery Q1. During an Anterior Approach (Hueter) to the hip joint, bleeding is encountered in the intermuscular plane between the Tensor Fasciae Latae (TFL) and Sartorius. Which vessel is most vulnerable to injury at this stage?
o: Ascending Branch of Lateral Femoral Circumflex Artery (LFCA)
First Perforating Artery of Profunda Femoris
items.e: [Ascending Branch of LFCA] The internervous plane for the direct anterior approach is between the TFL (Superior Gluteal N.) and Sartorius (Femoral N.). Deep in this interval, the ascending branch of the lateral femoral circumflex artery crosses horizontally and must be identified, ligated, or cauterized to prevent brisk arterial bleeding and postoperative hematoma formation.

items.q: According to Lewinnek's defined "Safe Zone" for acetabular cup positioning in THA to minimize post- operative dislocation, which pair of angles represents the exact standard target?
items.e: [Inclination: 40° ± 10°, Anteversion: 15° ± 10°] Lewinnek's classic safe zone defined acetabular cup inclination as 40° ± 10° (30° – 50°) and anteversion as 15° ± 10° (5° – 25°). Combined anteversion (femoral + acetabular) generally targets 25° – 45° to optimize stability and avoid impingement. High-Yield Reference Metric Master Table Anatomical / Surgical Parameter Standard Range / Target Value Clinical Significance Neck-Shaft Angle (NSA) 125° – 135° <125° causes Coxa Vara (increases femoral stem bending moment); >135° causes Coxa Valga. Hip Joint Reaction Force (Walking)

items.q: 5× to 4× Body Weight Increases up to 7 – 8× Body Weight during high-impact activities or stumbling. Lewinnek Cup Anteversion 15° ± 10° Malpositioning increases risks of anterior (excessive version) or posterior dislocation. Q-Angle (Females vs. Males) Females: ~14° – 17° | Males: ~10° – 14° Increased Q-angle increases lateral patellar tracking forces and patellofemoral arthritis. Section B: Total Knee Arthroplasty (TKA) & Revision Protocols Q3. A 68-year-old male with a history of primary TKA presents 4 years later with persistent knee pain, a felt "patellar clunk" when extending the knee from 60° to 30° flexion, and no systemic signs of infection. What is the underlying cause?
o: Loose Tibial Component with Anterior Subsidence
Fibrovascular Nodule Entrapment at the Superior Pole of the Patella
Excessive External Rotation of the Femoral Component
Patellar Tendon Rupture with Patellar Baja
items.e: [Fibrovascular Nodule Entrapment] Patellar clunk syndrome is caused by a fibrous/ fibrovascular nodule that forms at the junction of the superior pole of the patella and the quadriceps tendon. During knee flexion, the nodule lodges into the intercondylar notch of the posterior-stabilized (PS) femoral component, and during extension (around 30° – 45°), it abruptly pops out with a painful "clunk."

items.q: In Total Knee Arthroplasty, what is the consequence of placing the femoral component in excessive Internal Rotation?
o: Flexion gap asymmetry leading to lateral laxity and patellar maltracking
Flexion gap asymmetry leading to medial tightness and anterior impingement
Symmetric tightness in both extension and flexion gaps
Improved Q-angle leading to reduced patellar wear
items.e: [Flexion gap asymmetry leading to lateral laxity & patellar maltracking] Internal rotation of the femoral component narrows the medial flexion space and widens the lateral flexion space. It shifts the trochlear groove medially, thereby increasing the Q-angle and lateral forces, leading to patellar subluxation/maltracking, tilt, or polyethylene failure.

items.q: According to the MSIS (Musculoskeletal Infection Society) / ICM criteria for Periprosthetic Joint Infection (PJI), which of the following is considered a MAJOR criterion for diagnosis?
o: Elevated Synovial Fluid WBC Count > 3,000 cells/μL
Sinus Tract Communicating directly with the Prosthesis
items.e: [Sinus Tract Communicating directly with the Prosthesis] The two MAJOR criteria for PJI (where presence of either one is diagnostic) are: 1) Two positive operative synovial/tissue cultures with identical organisms, OR 2) A sinus tract communicating with the joint/prosthesis. Elevated CRP, high synovial WBC, or a single positive culture are minor criteria. High-Yield Exam Pearl: Vancouver Classification of Periprosthetic Femoral Fractures • Type A: Peritrochanteric region (AG = Greater Trochanter; AL = Lesser Trochanter). • Type B: Around or just distal to the stem. B1: Well- fixed stem (ORIF needed); B2: Loose stem, good bone stock (Revision with long stem); B3: Loose stem, poor bone stock (Revision with stem + allograft/strut). • Type C: Well distal to the stem tip (Treated independently with ORIF). Section C: Biomaterials, Wear Mechanisms & Tribology

items.q: Highly Cross-Linked Polyethylene (HXLPE) was introduced to reduce volumetric wear rate in total hip arthroplasty. What is the main structural trade-off or compromise caused by free-radical induced cross- linking and subsequent thermal annealing/remelting?
o: Reduction in mechanical tensile strength, yield strength, and fatigue resistance
Increased susceptibility to oxidative degradation in vivo
Marked increase in modulus of elasticity causing stress shielding
items.e: [Reduction in mechanical tensile strength, yield strength, and fatigue resistance] Radiation-induced cross-linking breaks polymer chains to form covalent cross-links, improving wear resistance. However, thermal processing (remelting/annealing) to eliminate residual free radicals reduces crystallinity, which compromises the tensile strength, ultimate yield strength, and fatigue propagation resistance of HXLPE.

items.q: A 62-year-old female undergoes THA with a Ceramic-on-Ceramic (CoC) bearing couple. 3 years postoperatively, she reports a loud, audible "squeaking" sound during gait. Which surgical parameter is most strongly correlated with this complication?
o: Micro-separation caused by steep cup inclination (> 50°) leading to edge loading
Incomplete seat engagement of the polyethylene liner
Use of a 28mm ceramic head size instead of 36mm
items.e: [Micro-separation caused by steep cup inclination (> 50°) leading to edge loading] Squeaking in Ceramic-on-Ceramic bearings is associated with fluid film breakdown and stripe wear caused by edge loading. Steep cup inclination (>50°), mal-anteversion, component mismatch, or pelvic tilting leads to micro-separation during heel-strike, stripe wear, and acoustical squeaking.

items.q: Which of the following orthopaedic biomaterials exhibits the highest Elastic Modulus (Young's Modulus, GPa), contributing most to proximal stress shielding in non-cemented femoral stems?
items.e: [Cobalt-Chromium-Molybdenum Alloy (Co-Cr-Mo)] Co-Cr alloys have a Young's modulus of ~210 – 240 GPa, compared to Stainless Steel (~200 GPa), Ti- 6Al-4V (~110 GPa), and cortical bone (12 – 18 GPa). A higher elastic modulus causes stiffer stems to carry more load, shielding the proximal femur from physiological stress and causing proximal bone resorption. Biomaterial Physical Properties Reference Matrix Biomaterial Elastic Modulus (GPa) Primary Wear Mode / Failure Mechanism Cortical Bone (Human) 12 – 18 GPa Physiological baseline for stiffness matching. Ti-6Al-4V Alloy 110 GPa Low shear strength; prone to fretting corrosion at modular junctions. Co-Cr-Mo Alloy 210 – 240 GPa High stiffness; potential metal-ion release (cobaltism/ALTR). Alumina Oxide Ceramic ~380 – 400 GPa Brittle fracture risk; squeaking with edge loading. Section D: Specialized Arthroplasty (UKA, RTSA & Revision TKA)

items.q: Which of the following is considered an ABSOLUTE CONTRAINDICATION for fixed-bearing Unicondylar Knee Arthroplasty (UKA) in medial compartment osteoarthritis?
o: Deficiency or chronic tear of the Anterior Cruciate Ligament (ACL)
items.e: [Deficiency or chronic tear of the ACL] An intact ACL is vital for UKA kinematics. ACL deficiency allows anterior tibial translation and shifted contact stress to the posterior tibial plateau, leading to rapid disease progression in the unreplaced lateral compartment and early implant loosening.

items.q: In Reverse Total Shoulder Arthroplasty (RTSA), moving the center of rotation (COR) medially and inferiorly alters shoulder biomechanics primarily by doing what?
o: Restoring supraspinatus tension and increasing subscapularis leverage
Lengthening the deltoid moment arm and recruiting deltoid fibers for elevation
Decreasing shear forces at the glenosphere-glenoid baseplate interface
Increasing external rotation power by pre-tensioning Teres Minor
items.e: [Lengthening the deltoid moment arm & recruiting deltoid fibers] RTSA shifts the center of rotation medially and inferiorly relative to the native glenohumeral joint. This increases the moment arm of the deltoid muscle and pre-tensions its fibers, enabling functional arm elevation in the presence of a deficient rotator cuff.

items.q: During revision TKA for a severe distal femoral bone defect involving the epicondyles (AORI Type III defect), which component constraint selection is required to provide joint stability?
o: Posterior Stabilized (PS) insert with long intramedullary stem
Cruciate Retaining (CR) design with offset stem
items.e: [Hinged (Rotating Hinge) Prosthesis] Epicondylar bone loss removes collateral ligament attachments (MCL/LCL). When collateral ligament integrity or peri-articular bone stock is completely compromised (AORI Type III), constrained or rotating- hinge implants are required to prevent gross coronal and sagittal instability. High-Yield Exam Pearl: Anderson Orthopaedic Research Institute (AORI) TKA Defect Classification • Type I (Minor): Intact metaphyseal bone; joint line unchanged; can be treated with standard augments or cement. • Type II (Metaphyseal): Damaged metaphyseal bone requiring modular augments, blocks, or sleeves/cones (2A: single condyle; 2B: both condyles). • Type III (Deficient Metaphysis/Collaterals): Massive bone loss involving epicondyles/collaterals; requires structural allograft, porous metal cones, and constrained hinged implants. Section E: Advanced THA Complications & Biomechanical Failures

items.q: A 65-year-old male presents with deep groin pain 5 years after a bilateral Metal-on-Metal (MoM) THA. MRI reveals a solid pseudotumor surrounding the acetabulum without osseous destruction. Synovial fluid aspiration shows elevated Cobalt (18 ppb) and Chromium (14 ppb) levels. What is the characteristic histological finding of Adverse Local Tissue Reaction (ALTR / ALAVAL) in this patient?
o: Abundant foreign-body giant cells filled with polyethylene wear debris
Perivascular lymphocytic in filtrates (ALAVAL pattern) with tissue necrosis
Acute neutrophilic infiltration with fibrinopurulent exudate
Granulomatous inflammation with Langhans giant cells and caseation
items.e: [Perivascular lymphocytic in filtrates (ALAVAL pattern) with tissue necrosis] Aseptic Lymphocyte-dominated Vasculitis-Associated Lesions (ALAVAL) are the classic histological hallmark of ALTR/pseudotumors caused by metal-on-metal wear or severe trunnionosis. Histology shows perivascular T- and B-lymphocytic aggregation, macrophage infiltration laden with metallic wear particles, and extensive soft tissue necrosis.

items.q: In Paprosky classification of acetabular bone loss during revision THA, Type III-B defects are characterized by which specific radiographic and anatomical parameters?
o: Superior ischial lysis < 1 cm, teardrop intact, minimal superior migration
Severe Kohler's line break, superior migration > 3 cm, ischial lysis > 2 cm, high risk of pelvic discontinuity
Moderate Kohler's line disruption, superior migration 1 – 3 cm, intact teardrop
Intact acetabular rim with central cavitary defect only
items.e: [Severe Kohler's line break, superior migration > 3 cm, ischial lysis > 2 cm, pelvic discontinuity] Paprosky III-B represents severe up-and-in acetabular destruction: superior migration > 3 cm, severe ischial osteolysis (> 2 cm below teardrop), complete destruction of Kohler's line (ilioischial line break), and involvement of > 60% of the acetabular ring/columns, frequently accompanied by pelvic discontinuity.

items.q: In cementless THA, proximal femoral "Stress Shielding" (Grumbridge/Engh classification) occurs primarily due to which mechanical phenomenon?
o: Micromotion at the bone-prosthesis interface > 150 μm preventing osseointegration
Load transfer occurring predominantly distally in a diaphyseal-engaging stiff stem, leaving the calcar unloaded
Interfacial thermal necrosis from exothermic PMMA polymerization
Excessive head size leading to increased frictional torque on the trunnion
items.e: [Load transfer occurring predominantly distally in a diaphyseal-engaging stem] Wolff's law states bone remodels in response to stress. When a stiff, fully hydroxyapatite-coated or porous-coated stem achieves rigid fixation distally in the diaphysis, the mechanical loads bypass the proximal metaphyseal bone/calcar. Unloaded bone undergoes proximal resorptive bone loss (stress shielding). Paprosky Acetabular Bone Loss Classification Summary Type Superior Migration Ischial Osteolysis Kohler's Line Surgical Reconstruction Strategy Type I None None Intact Standard hemispherical cementless cup Type II (A- C) Mild (< 2 cm) Mild / None Intact / Minimal Jumbo cup, particulate graft, or modular augments Type III-A Moderate (2 – 3 cm) Moderate (< 1.5 cm) Intact Trabecular metal augments + cup / structural graft Section F: Complex TKA Alignment & Kinematics

items.q: Kinematic Alignment (KA) in Total Knee Arthroplasty differs fundamentally from Mechanical Alignment (MA) by targeting which anatomical axis alignment goal?
o: Cutting distal femur and proximal tibia perpendicular (90°) to their respective mechanical axes
Restoring the patient's constitutional pre-arthritic joint line orientation and natural laxity without ligament release
Creating a 3° varus tibial cut and 3° valgus distal femoral cut in every patient regardless of native anatomy
Standardizing the coronal plane alignment to 0° HKA (Hip-Knee-Ankle) angle in all individuals
items.e: [Restoring constitutional pre-arthritic joint line orientation and laxity] Kinematic alignment aims to resurface the joint to match the individual patient's constitutional pre- arthritic joint line and rotational axes, preserving physiological soft-tissue tension without performing extensive ligamentous releases. In contrast, Mechanical Alignment forces every knee into a neutral 0° mechanical axis (90° cuts to bone axes).

items.q: During TKA gap balancing, a knee is found to be properly balanced in extension but excessively TIGHT in flexion. Which surgical resection adjustment will selectively increase the flexion space without altering the extension space?
o: Increasing posterior femoral condylar resection (posterior cut) or reducing femoral component size
Recutting the distal femur with 2° of additional flexion
items.e: [Increasing posterior femoral resection / downsizing femoral component] The flexion gap is created between the posterior femoral condyles and the proximal tibial cut. Increasing posterior femoral resection (or downsizing the femoral component without anterior notch creation) enlarges the flexion gap selectively without affecting extension. Distal femoral cuts affect ONLY the extension space.

items.q: In Total Knee Arthroplasty, raising the joint line (joint line elevation > 5 mm) due to excessive distal femoral resection compensated by a thicker poly spacer leads to which clinical complication?
o: Patellar Baja, reduced quadriceps moment arm, and flexion tightness
items.e: Over-resecting the distal femur and filling the extension gap with a thicker insert raises the joint line. The patella then sits low relative to the new joint line (pseudo-patella baja, with patellofemoral impingement), and the altered collateral ligament isometry causes mid-flexion instability. True patella baja (option B) comes from patellar tendon shortening, not joint-line elevation.

items.q: In the Paprosky Classification of Femoral Bone Defects during revision THA, a Type III-B defect is best described by which structural characteristic?
o: Intact metaphysis with minimal osteolysis providing complete proximal support
Metaphyseal bone loss with intact diaphysis offering > 4 cm of intact diaphyseal bone for stem scratch fit
Severe metaphyseal-diapseal bone loss with < 4 cm of intact diaphyseal bone, requiring modular tapered fluted titanium stems or impaction grafting
Complete loss of cortical integrity from the metaphysis to the distal femur, requiring an allograft-prosthesis composite or total femur replacement
items.e: [Severe loss with < 4 cm intact diaphysis] Paprosky Type III-B femoral defects feature extensive metaphyseal and proximal diaphyseal osteolysis where less than 4 cm of intact diaphyseal canal remains for distal fixation. Type III-A has > 4 cm of intact diaphysis. Type III-B defects typically require modular tapered fluted stems that achieve distal bypass fixation.

items.q: During Femoral Impaction Bone Grafting (IBG) in revision total hip arthroplasty, which bone graft preparation yields optimal structural stability and mechanical interlocking?
o: Fine ground bone slurry (< 1 mm) without washed marrow lipids
Morselized cancellous bone chips sized 8 – 10 mm, thoroughly washed of fat and blood content, tightly impacted
Large cortical struts > 30 mm placed strictly inside the medullary canal without cancellous packing
Unwashed morselized graft mixed in a 1:1 ratio with liquid PMMA cement
items.e: [Morselized cancellous chips 8 – 10 mm, washed of fat/blood] According to the Exeter protocol for IBG, optimal graft stability requires washing fat/lipids out of the cancellous chips and using a particle size of 8 – 10 mm. Washed graft increases the coefficient of friction and shear strength between particles when impacted, providing a stable bed for cemented stem fixation.

items.q: What is the primary function of a Femoral Sleeve or Cone in Revision Total Knee Arthroplasty when addressing AORI Type II or III metaphyseal bone loss?
o: To bypass the joint completely and transfer all load into the diaphysis via a long un-cemented stem
To achieve zone 2 (metaphyseal) axial and rotational fixation, converting shear forces to compressive loads
To serve purely as a spacer without providing structural mechanical support
To reinforce patellar tendon re-attachment at the tibial tubercle
items.e: [Achieve zone 2 metaphyseal axial/rotational fixation] The Morgan-Jones zonal fixation concept divides revision knee stability into 3 zones: Zone 1 (Epiphysis), Zone 2 (Metaphysis), and Zone 3 (Diaphysis). Metaphyseal sleeves and porous titanium cones establish robust Zone 2 fixation, transferring structural loads to host metaphyseal bone and protecting joint line reconstruction. items.q: A 72-year-old male with a history of right TKA performed 8 weeks ago presents with a acute 4-day history of severe knee pain, joint effusion, and fever. Synovial fluid aspiration yields 65,000 WBC/μL with 92% neutrophils. The implant is well- fixed without component loosening. What is the standard operative treatment strategy?
o: Single-stage exchange arthroplasty with antibiotic PMMA cement
Debridement, Antibiotic Retention, and Implant Exchange (DAIR) with modular liner exchange
Two-stage exchange arthroplasty with placement of an articulating spacer
Long-term suppressive oral antibiotic therapy without surgical intervention
items.e: [DAIR with modular liner exchange] DAIR is indicated for acute PJI (symptoms < 3 weeks OR occurring within 4 weeks of index surgery) with well- fixed components, mature soft-tissue envelope, and absence of sinus tract. Modular liner exchange allows access to the posterior capsule for thorough synovectomy and decontamination of hidden bacterial bio films.

items.q: In two-stage revision arthroplasty for chronic Periprosthetic Joint Infection, what is the key advantage of an ARTICULATING antibiotic spacer over a STATIC spacer?
o: Significantly higher local elution rate of aminoglycosides and vancomycin
Maintenance of soft-tissue envelope length, preservation of ROM, and easier re-exposure during stage 2
Complete elimination of mechanical shear stress across host bone interfaces
Elimination of systemic toxicity from antibiotic PMMA leaching
items.e: [Maintenance of soft-tissue envelope length & easier re-exposure] Articulating antibiotic spacers maintain joint space height, preserve collateral ligament tension, reduce quadriceps shortening/arthrofibrosis, and improve functional mobility between stages. This significantly facilitates surgical exposure and dissection during the second-stage reimplantation.

items.q: In Image-Free (Haptic / Inertial) Robotic-Assisted Total Knee Arthroplasty, how does the system register bone landmarks and establish virtual surgical registration intraoperatively?
o: Preoperative 3D CT scan matched to intraoperative fluoroscopic projections
Optical tracker arrays attached to femur and tibia combined with anatomical point-probe mapping
Intraoperative ultrasound transducer arrays placed along the joint capsule
Preoperative full-leg standing digital X-ray calibrated with a radiopaque sphere
items.e: [Optical tracker arrays + point-probe anatomical mapping] Image-free robotic systems utilize rigid body arrays with infrared optical spheres attached to the femur and tibia. The surgeon uses a tracked digitizing probe to paint the articular surfaces and register specific anatomical landmarks (center of femoral head, epicondyles, tibial center), creating a real-time kinematic profile without requiring a preoperative CT scan. High-Yield Exam Pearl: Zonal Fixation in Revision Arthroplasty (Morgan-Jones Concept) • Zone 1 (Epiphyseal/Joint Surface): Reconstructed with augments, offset adapters, or impaction graft. • Zone 2 (Metaphyseal): Primary area for load transfer using porous metal cones or titanium sleeves. • Zone 3 (Diaphyseal): Provides rotational alignment and alignment stability via cementlessfluted stems or cemented smooth stems. Successful revision requires solid engagement in at least TWO of the three zones. items.q: During an Anterior Approach (Hueter) to the hip joint, bleeding is encountered in the intermuscular plane between the Tensor Fasciae Latae (TFL) and Sartorius. Which vessel is most vulnerable to injury at this stage?
o: Ascending Branch of Lateral Femoral Circumflex Artery (LFCA)
First Perforating Artery of Profunda Femoris
items.e: [Ascending Branch of LFCA] The internervous plane for the direct anterior approach is between the TFL (Superior Gluteal N.) and Sartorius (Femoral N.). Deep in this interval, the ascending branch of the lateral femoral circumflex artery crosses horizontally and must be identified, ligated, or cauterized to prevent brisk arterial bleeding and postoperative hematoma formation.

items.q: During a primary TKA, after completing distal femoral and proximal tibial resections, you assess the joint gaps with a spacer block. The gap is found to be tight in extension, but perfectly balanced in flexion. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step?
items.e: Resect additional distal femur. Distal femoral resection directly impacts ONLY the extension gap without altering the flexion gap. Resecting additional proximal tibia increases both flexion and extension gaps. Releasing the posterior capsule is reserved for fixed flexion deformities when bone cuts are completed.

items.q: In a TKA for a severe fixed valgus deformity (>15 degrees), which of the following sequences of lateral soft tissue releases is considered standard practice?
items.e: Osteophytes → ITB subperiosteal → Popliteus / LCL. Removal of osteophytes is always the FIRST step in soft-tissue balancing. For valgus knees: ITB release corrects tightness mainly in extension; Popliteus release corrects tightness mainly in flexion; LCL release corrects tightness in both. Over-release of LCL/Popliteus necessitates a constrained liner.

items.q: A patient undergoing TKA has a pre-operative fixed flexion deformity (FFD) of 25°. Which step is essential during femoral component positioning to avoid flexion-gap tightness?
o: Downsize the femoral component and shift anteriorly
Upsize the femoral component with posterior augmentation
Ensure adequate posterior femoral condylar resection and posterior capsular release
items.e: Ensure adequate posterior femoral condylar resection and posterior capsular release. FFD requires bone resections that restore extension space (e.g., additional distal femur cut, posterior osteophyte resection, posterior capsular strip, and release of gastrocnemius heads). Under-resecting posterior condyles compromises flexion space and produces flexion tightness. High-Yield Rule for TKA Gap Balancing: Tight in Extension & Flexion: Resect more proximal tibia or use thinner tibial insert. Tight in Extension ONLY: Resect more distal femur or release posterior capsule. Tight in Flexion ONLY: Recess posterior cruciate ligament (PCL), increase posterior femoral slope, or downsize femoral component. TOTAL HIP ARTHROPLASTY (THA): BIOMECHANICS, ORIENTATIONS & TRIBOLOGY

items.q: What are the classical Lewinnek safe zones for acetabular cup orientation in primary Total Hip Arthroplasty?
items.e: Inclination: 40° ± 10° (30° – 50°), Anteversion: 15° ± 10° (5° – 25°). Standard safe zones established by Lewinnek minimize posterior dislocation and edge loading. Current functional positioning concepts also account for spinomedicular pelvic tilt (pelvic tilt increases by ~1° for every 1° of lumbar flexion).

items.q: According to Wasielewski's quadrant system for acetabular cup screw fixation, which quadrant is designated as the SAFE zone to avoid vascular and neurological injury?
items.e: Posterosuperior quadrant. A line from the anterior superior iliac spine (ASIS) through the center of the acetabulum divides it into anterior and posterior halves. The Posterosuperior quadrant allows secure screw purchase into thick iliac bone without risking external iliac vessels (anterosuperior) or obturator vessels/nerve (anteroinferior).

items.q: In ceramic-on-ceramic (CoC) bearing surfaces in total hip arthroplasty, "squeaking" is most closely linked to which mechanical phenomenon?
o: Edge loading and loss of fluid- film lubrication
Oxidation of ultra-high molecular weight polyethylene
items.e: Edge loading and loss of fluid- film lubrication. Ceramic bearings rely on fluid- film lubrication. Micro-separation, cup steepness (>50° inclination), or impingement breaks this fluid film, causing stripe wear and high-frequency acoustical vibration ("squeaking"). Volumetric wear in CoC is extremely low (<1 mm³/year). items.q: According to the 2018 Musculoskeletal Infection Society (MSIS) / International Consensus Meeting (ICM) criteria, which of the following constitutes a MAJOR diagnostic criterion for Periprosthetic Joint Infection (PJI)?
o: Presence of a sinus tract communicating with the prosthesis
items.e: Presence of a sinus tract communicating with the prosthesis. MSIS/ICM criteria define 2 MAJOR criteria (either is diagnostic of PJI): 1) Sinus tract communicating with the joint; OR 2) Two positive identical pre-operative or intra-operative cultures. Serum CRP, synovial WBC, and alpha-defensin form minor scoring criteria.

items.q: A 72-year-old female presents 4 years post-primary cementless THA following a fall. Radiographs show a fracture around the tip of a well- fixed femoral stem with moderate bone stock degradation. According to the Vancouver classification, how is this fracture categorized and managed?
o: Vancouver Type B1; Revision with long uncemented stem
Vancouver Type B1; Open reduction and internal fixation (ORIF) with plate & cables
Vancouver Type B2; ORIF with locking plate alone
items.e: Vancouver Type B1; ORIF with plate & cables. Vancouver Type B1 fractures occur around or just distal to the stem with a WELL-FIXED stem . Treatment is ORIF with locked plating and strut allografts/cables. Type B2 (loose stem, good bone) requires revision arthroplasty with a long stem. Type B3 (loose stem, poor bone) requires revision with fluted tapered stem or proximal femoral replacement.

items.q: Which organism is most commonly associated with early acute PJI (<4 weeks post-op) and is known for biofilm formation that makes DAIR (Debridement, Antibiotics, and Implant Retention) challenging without specific anti-biofilm agents?
items.e: Staphylococcus aureus / Staphylococcus epidermidis. Staphylococci produce exopolysaccharide slime layer bio films on metal/polyethylene implants. Rifampicin is added to antimicrobial regimens specifically for its ability to penetrate Staphylococcal bio films during DAIR procedures. Summary: Vancouver Classification of Periprosthetic Femoral Fractures Type A: Trochanteric region (AG = Greater Trochanter, AL = Lesser Trochanter). Rx: Conservative or tension-band. Type B1: Around/distal to stem; Stem WELL-FIXED . Rx: ORIF (Plate + Cables ± Strut). Type B2: Around/distal to stem; Stem LOOSE , bone adequate. Rx: Revision to long uncemented stem. Type B3: Around/distal to stem; Stem LOOSE , poor bone stock. Rx: Revision stem / Proximal Femoral Replacement. Type C: Well distal to stem tip. Rx: ORIF independently of prosthesis. items.q: In revision TKA with massive uncontained metaphyseal bone defects (AORI Type III), which reconstructive modality provides the highest rate of biological osseointegration and structural fixation?
o: Highly porous titanium / Tantalum metaphyseal sleeves or cones
items.e: Highly porous titanium / Tantalum metaphyseal sleeves or cones. Porous tantalum/titanium cones and sleeves achieve zonal fixation in Zone 2 (metaphysis), bypassing damaged Zone 1 (epiphysis). Structural allografts carry risks of late collapse and non-union, whereas cement alone exhibits high failure rates in large uncontained defects.

items.q: A patient with severe recurvatum deformity (>15°) undergoes revision TKA. To correct the recurvatum and prevent hyperextension instability, which strategy is most appropriate?
o: Resect additional distal femur and insert a thinner polyethylene
Proximalize the femoral component, augment distal femur, and increase posterior tibial slope
Distalize the joint line by augmenting the distal femur and using a thicker polyethylene insert
Release the posterior capsule and Gastrocnemius insertion
items.e: Distalize the joint line by augmenting the distal femur and using a thicker polyethylene insert. Hyperextension/recurvatum results from excessive extension space. Distalizing the femoral component (using distal femoral augments) and increasing poly thickness tightens the extension space and restores the joint line without compromising the flexion gap.

items.q: During revision TKA, an stem is added to the tibial component. According to engineering principles, what percentage of axial load is transmitted through a fully engaged offset/press- fit stem away from the metaphysis?
items.e: 30% – 50%. Diaphyseal stem engagement stress-shields the surrounding bone by transferring 30% to 50% of the axial load away from the proximal tibia into the diaphysis, protecting metaphyseal bone grafts or cones during healing.

items.q: What is the principal mechanical disadvantage of using a rotating-hinge knee prosthesis in revision TKA compared to a constrained condylar knee (CCK) insert?
o: Increased shear stress transmission to the bone-implant interface leading to aseptic loosening
Increased incidence of patellar tendon rupture
items.e: Increased shear stress transmission to the bone-implant interface leading to aseptic loosening. Highly constrained implants (hinges) restrict degrees of freedom and transfer massive torsional and varus-valgus lever forces directly to the stem-bone interface, increasing long-term aseptic loosening risk.

items.q: According to the Paprosky Classification of Acetabular Bone Loss in Revision THA, which type is characterized by total loss of the posterior column and superior migration >3 cm with pelvic discontinuity?
items.e: Type IIIB. Paprosky Type IIIB involves severe acetabular rim destruction (>60%), loss of posterior column, teardrop osteolysis, and >3 cm superior hip center migration with high risk of pelvic discontinuity. Type IIIA has >3 cm migration but intact posterior column supporting cup stability.

items.q: In managing a true pelvic discontinuity during revision THA with Paprosky Type IIIB defects, which structural construct offers the highest stability?
o: Jumbo acetabular cup with 2 trans- fixation screws
Cemented cup inside an impaction bone graft bed
Cup-cage construct or Custom triflange acetabular component (CTAC)
Standalone porous tantalum augment without posterior column plating
items.e: Cup-cage construct or Custom triflange acetabular component (CTAC). Pelvic discontinuity separates upper and lower pelvis. Fixation requires bridging the defect onto ilium and ischium using a cup-cage construct, custom 3D printed triflange implant, or distraction with modular tantalum cages.

items.q: During revision THA, a extended trochanteric osteotomy (ETO) is performed to remove a firmly fixed stem. What is the maximum recommended length of an ETO measured from the tip of the greater trochanter?
items.e: 12 – 15 cm. An ETO should provide exposure while preserving at least 5 to 7 cm of intact distal diaphyseal bone for press- fit fixation of the revision fluted tapered stem. It is typically 12 – 15 cm measured from the tip of the greater trochanter.

items.q: Which modular femoral revision stem design demonstrates the lowest rate of subsidence in Paprosky Type IIIB femoral bone defects?
o: Splined, fluted, tapered titanium stem (Conical taper 2° to 3°)
items.e: Splined, fluted, tapered titanium stem (Conical taper 2° to 3°). Modular fluted tapered stems rely on splines to engage diaphyseal bone and provide rotational stability, while the taper provides vertical wedge stability. They achieve superior scratch fit in deficient diaphyses compared to cylindrical stems.

items.q: Dual-mobility acetabular constructs significantly reduce dislocation rates in revision THA. What is the primary mechanism of dual-mobility bearings?
o: Increasing the offset of the abductor muscle mechanism by 15 mm
Increasing the effective head size and jump distance while retaining a small inner femoral head diameter
Completely locking the liner inside the metal shell
items.e: Increasing the effective head size and jump distance. Dual mobility features two articulation points: inner head inside a large poly liner, and outer poly liner inside the smooth shell. This offers a large jump distance (distance the femoral head must travel to dislocate) while maintaining low volumetric wear. SECTION 3: PERIPROSTHETIC FRACTURES & FIXATION STRATEGIES (Q11 – Q15)

items.q: A 68-year-old male presents with a periprosthetic knee fracture involving the distal femur around a well- fixed PS femoral component (Supracondylar Felix/Lewis Type II). Which construct is the gold standard treatment?
o: Immediate revision to a distal femoral replacement (DFR)
Retrograde intramedullary nail or distal femoral lateral locking compression plate (LCP)
Long leg cast immobilization for 8 weeks
Tension band wiring with cerclage cables
items.e: Retrograde intramedullary nail or distal femoral lateral locking compression plate (LCP). If the prosthesis is stable/well- fixed, fixation with a locked plate or retrograde nail (if the box of the PS component allows passage) is indicated. Revision to DFR is reserved for loose implants or severe comminuted non-reconstructable bone loss.

items.q: According to the UCS (Unified Classification System) for periprosthetic fractures, how is a fracture occurring in a bone containing an implant, but NOT surrounding the implant (e.g., intertrochanteric fracture above an ipsilateral TKA stem), classified?
items.e: Class C. In the Unified Classification System (Duncan and Haddad), type C is a fracture clear of the implant in a bone that contains one, such as a fracture well away from a TKA femoral component. B is around or next to an implant (B1 well fixed, B2 loose, B3 poor bone), D divides a bone between two implants, E involves each of two bones supporting one arthroplasty, F is an unreplaced joint surface articulating with an implant (e.g. the acetabulum opposite a hemiarthroplasty), and A is apophyseal or extra-articular (e.g. greater trochanter).

items.q: In periprosthetic acetabular fractures associated with THA, which factor is the single most critical determinant in deciding between ORIF and revision arthroplasty?
o: Stability/ fixation status of the acetabular cup
Use of cemented vs. uncemented cup
items.e: Stability/ fixation status of the acetabular cup. Like femoral periprosthetic fractures, cup stability dictates management. If the cup is stable (Della Valle Type I/II), non- operative or ORIF is chosen. If loose (Della Valle Type III/IV), revision of the acetabular shell is required.

items.q: Intraoperative fracture of the medial malleolus during TKA is best managed intraoperatively by which technique?
o: Tension band wiring or partially threaded cannulated cancellous screw fixation
Revision to a constrained hinge knee
items.e: Tension band wiring or partially threaded cancellous screw fixation. Intraoperative fracture of the medial malleolus compromises the deltoid ligament attachment, causing severe acute ankle/tibial instability. Rigid internal fixation with CC screws or tension band wiring is required immediately.

items.q: A periprosthetic fracture occurs at the anterior notch of the distal femoral cortex created during primary TKA. What degree of anterior femoral cortical notching increases the risk of fracture by >40%?
o: Cortical notching does not alter fracture risk
items.e: Notch depth > 3 mm (or >25% cortical thickness). Anterior femoral cortical notching creates a local stress riser. Biomechanical studies confirm that notches >3 mm significantly reduce torsional strength of the distal femur by 29% to 40%. SECTION 4: PJI DIAGNOSTICS, ANTIBIOTIC SPACERS & MANAGEMENT (Q16 – Q20)

items.q: What is the recommended concentration of Vancomycin per 40g bag of PMMA bone cement when fabricating a HIGH-DOSE therapeutic antibiotic bone spacer for a two-stage revision THA/TKA?
items.e: 3 to 4 grams per 40g cement. Prophylactic cement contains ≤ 1g antibiotic per 40g batch (preserves mechanical strength). Therapeutic antibiotic spacers require high elution: 3 – 4g Vancomycin + 2 – 4g Tobramycin/Gentamicin per 40g PMMA bag.

items.q: In the DAIR (Debridement, Antibiotics, and Implant Retention) procedure for acute PJI, which of the following steps is MANDATORY to maximize treatment success?
o: Retaining the original modular polyethylene insert to prevent joint instability
Exchange of all modular components (polyethylene insert, femoral head)
Performing the procedure only after 8 weeks of systemic oral antibiotics
items.e: Exchange of all modular components (polyethylene insert, femoral head). Exchanging modular components allows access to the posterior capsule and underlying interfaces to clear biofilm buildup, significantly increasing DAIR success rate from <50% to >80%.

items.q: A synovial fluid biomarker test shows elevated Alpha-defensin. What is the sensitivity and specificity of the Alpha-defensin immunoassay in diagnosing PJI?
items.e: Sensitivity >95%, Specificity >95%. Alpha-defensin is an antimicrobial peptide released by neutrophils in response to pathogens. It is resistant to prior antibiotic therapy interference and maintains high accuracy (>95% sensitivity and specificity).

items.q: What is the ideal timing for obtaining pre-operative joint aspiration for culture in a patient suspected of PJI who is currently receiving oral antibiotic therapy?
o: Aspiration should be performed immediately without stopping antibiotics
Antibiotics should be withheld for at least 2 weeks prior to aspiration
Antibiotics should be stopped for 24 hours prior to aspiration
Aspiration is contraindicated if antibiotics were given within 6 months
items.e: Antibiotics should be withheld for at least 2 weeks prior to aspiration. Active antibiotic therapy inhibits organism growth in culture media, causing false-negative synovial fluid cultures. A 2-week antibiotic-free window (drug holiday) is required before diagnostic joint aspiration.

items.q: In two-stage revision arthroplasty for PJI, what is the minimum duration of targeted systemic antibiotic therapy recommended before considering re-implantation?
items.e: 4 to 6 weeks. The standard international guideline specifies 4 – 6 weeks of targeted pathogen-specific antibiotic therapy (often IV initially, followed by high-bioavailability oral agents) prior to clinical re-evaluation for stage two re-implantation. SECTION 5: BIOMATERIALS, TRIBOLOGY & HIGH-YIELD CORE (Q21 – Q25)

items.q: What process in highly cross-linked polyethylene (HXLPE) manufacturing reduces free radical oxidation and long-term wear while preserving mechanical strength?
o: Thermal annealing/remelting or Vitamin E (alpha- tocopherol) stabilization
Ethylene oxide gas sterilization without radiation
items.e: Thermal annealing/remelting or Vitamin E stabilization. Irradiation creates cross-links that reduce wear, but leaves free radicals that react with oxygen and cause degradation. Remelting/annealing or diffusing Vitamin E quenches free radicals, preventing oxidative degradation.

items.q: "Trunnionosis" in THA refers to mechanically assisted crevice corrosion (MACC) at which implant interface?
items.e: Femoral head-stem taper interface (12/14 taper). Trunnionosis occurs at the head-neck taper junction due to micromotion, fretting, and fluid ingress, releasing Co and Cr ions that trigger adverse local tissue reactions (ALTR) or pseudotumors.

items.q: Which bone cement additive alters PMMA polymer polymerization by acting as an initiator to start the exothermic reaction?
items.e: Benzoyl peroxide. Benzoyl peroxide in the powder acts as the initiator, reactivated by N,N-dimethyl-p-toluidine in the liquid monomer. Hydroquinone acts as an inhibitor to prevent premature polymerization during storage.

items.q: In ceramic-on-ceramic THA, what is the most common cause of catastrophic ceramic liner or head fracture?
o: Liner mipseating during impaction or edge loading from steep cup inclination (>50°)
items.e: Liner mipseating during impaction or edge loading. Mipseating creates stress concentrations along the ceramic rim. When combined with steep inclination (>50°), localized point loading exceeds the yield strength of alumina/zirconia toughened alumina, triggering brittle fracture.

items.q: Which implant alloy has the elastic modulus closest to human cortical bone (~15 – 20 GPa), minimizing stress shielding?
items.e: Beta-Titanium alloys (~40 – 55 GPa). Standard Ti-6Al-4V has a modulus of ~110 GPa. Newer Beta-Titanium alloys reduce this to ~40 – 55 GPa, closer to cortical bone (15 – 20 GPa), significantly reducing distal stress shielding and proximal femoral thigh pain. items.q: A 63‑year‑old male presents with groin pain 4 months after a cemented total hip arthroplasty. Radiographs show a radiolucent line at the bone‑cement interface but no subsidence of the femoral stem. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
items.e: A radiolucent line at the bone‑cement interface without subsidence is classic for aseptic loosening.

items.q: Which sterilisation method for polyethylene does NOT generate free radicals that require subsequent antioxidant treatment?
items.e: Gamma irradiation in nitrogen does not produce free radicals, unlike the other methods.

items.q: A 45‑year‑old woman with osteonecrosis of the femoral head is scheduled for a femoral head replacement. Which implant material should be avoided as a femoral head bearing surface because of poor wear resistance and notch sensitivity?
items.e: Titanium alloy has poor wear resistance and notch sensitivity, making it unsuitable as a head bearing surface.

items.q: A 70‑year‑old man develops a loud audible squeak during gait 3 years after a ceramic‑on‑ceramic total hip replacement. Which surgical parameter is most strongly correlated with this complication?
o: Incomplete seating of the polyethylene liner
28 mm ceramic head instead of 36 mm
items.e: Squeaking in ceramic‑on‑ceramic bearings is most strongly associated with steep cup inclination (> 50°) causing edge loading.

items.q: Which of the following is NOT a characteristic of highly cross‑linked polyethylene (HXLPE) manufactured by remelting?
items.e: Remelting reduces free radicals but does not increase wear resistance; it may reduce fracture toughness.

items.q: A 52‑year‑old patient with a history of long lumbar fusion now presents with low back pain and hip instability. The most important spinopelvic consideration after the fusion is that the pelvis cannot tilt posteriorly, thereby reducing functional cup anteversion. This statement reflects the fact that the pelvis:
o: Loses its ability to tilt in all directions
items.e: After a long lumbar fusion the pelvis cannot tilt posteriorly, which reduces functional cup anteversion and increases dislocation risk.

items.q: Which of the following materials shows almost no plastic deformation before failure, i.e., is classified as brittle?
items.e: Ceramics such as bone exhibit brittle behaviour, with little plastic deformation before failure.

items.q: Which of the following is the most common metal sensitiser in the general population?
items.e: The most common metal sensitiser in the general population is nickel.

items.q: Which alloying element in cobalt‑chromium‑molybdenum alloys primarily forms a passive oxide layer that resists corrosion?
items.e: Chromium forms a passive chromium oxide layer that improves corrosion resistance.

items.q: In a cemented femoral stem, the third‑generation cementing technique involves all of the following EXCEPT:
o: Use of a distal canal plug
Vacuum mixing to reduce porosity and improve centralisation
items.e: Third‑generation cementing uses vacuum mixing and centralisers; retrograde cement gun insertion is not a feature of this technique.

items.q: In a 24‑year‑old male who sustained a midshaft femoral fracture, the surgeon chooses a titanium interlocking nail. Upon reaming, the surgeon notices a thin, lamellated cortical layer on the medullary canal. Which property of titanium alloys makes them unsuitable as a femoral head bearing surface, as stated in the source text?
o: Poor wear resistance and notch sensitivity
items.e: Titanium alloy is unsuitable as a femoral head bearing mainly because of poor wear (abrasion) resistance and notch sensitivity.

items.q: A patient is being prepared for a total knee arthroplasty. The target tibial polyethylene thickness should be at least what measurement, according to the source?
items.e: The minimum recommended tibial polyethylene thickness in TKA is about 8 mm.

items.q: A 68‑year‑old woman with a history of long‑term steroid use wants a hip arthroplasty. Which metal sensitiser is most common in the general population, as per the source?
items.e: The most common metal sensitiser in the general population is Nickel.

items.q: During the direct anterior hip approach, which vessel is routinely ligated to prevent bleeding?
o: Ascending branch of the lateral circumflex femoral vessels
items.e: In the direct anterior approach the ascending branch of the lateral circumflex femoral vessels is typically ligated.

items.q: A 71‑year‑old man has a long lumbar fusion and now needs a THA. Which biomechanical concept explains his increased dislocation risk?
o: The pelvis cannot tilt posteriorly on sitting, reducing functional cup anteversion
items.e: A long lumbar fusion limits posterior pelvic tilt on sitting, decreasing functional cup anteversion and increasing dislocation risk.

items.q: What is the primary decelerative factor that a femoral head fracture revision should avoid, as listed in the source?
o: Using a ceramic head directly on a mildly damaged trunnion
Using a ceramic head with a titanium adapter sleeve
Applying bone cement on the taper
items.e: When the trunnion is mildly damaged, a ceramic head should not be used directly; a metal head is recommended.

items.q: A patient develops a periprosthetic joint infection. Which investigation measures free radicals associated with polyethylene oxidation and thus is NOT suitable for sterilisation of polyethylene?
items.e: Gamma irradiation in air generates free radicals; nitrogen reduces them.

items.q: During a direct lateral approach, excessive splitting of which muscle increases the risk of superior gluteal nerve injury?
o: Gluteus medius more than 10 cm above the tip of the greater trochanter
Gluteus medius more than 1 cm above the tip
Gluteus medius more than 5 cm above the tip
At the level of the lesser trochanter
items.e: Splitting gluteus medius more than 10 cm above the greater trochanter risks the superior gluteal nerve.

items.q: What is the approximate elastic modulus of a cobalt‑chromium‑molybdenum alloy relative to titanium, as inferred from the source?
items.e: Cobalt‑chromium alloys have a higher elastic modulus compared to titanium alloys.

items.q: Which of the following statements about bone cement is FALSE according to the source?
o: Cement setting time is shortened by increased ambient temperature
Barium sulphate is a radiopacifier in commercial cement
Nerve injury is the most common complication of cementation
items.e: The source does not state nerve injury as a common complication; cement is strongest in compression, setting time shortened by temperature and barium sulphate is a radiopacifier.

items.q: In a patient who has received a ceramic head after a head fracture, what is the recommended bearing for revision?
o: Ceramic head with sleeve and synovectomy
items.e: Revision after ceramic head fracture should use a ceramic head (with sleeve) and thorough synovectomy.

items.q: Which type of wear particle from metal-on-metal bearings is most clinically relevant, per the source?
items.e: Metal‑on‑metal wear particles are typically nanometre‑sized (about 10‑50 nm).

items.q: A 55‑year‑old male had a total knee arthroplasty with a proximally fixed, distally cemented femoral stem. What is the most common mechanism of fatigue fracture of a cemented femoral stem?
o: Proximal loss of support with a well‑fixed distal stem (cantilever bending)
items.e: The classic fatigue fracture mechanism is proximal loss of support with a well‑fixed distal stem, acting as a cantilever.

items.q: A 62‑year‑old male presents with a femoral shaft fracture 4 weeks post–cemented THA; radiographs show a short diaphyseal fragment adjacent to a well‑fixed femoral stem. According to the Vancouver classification, this fracture is best managed with:
o: Excision of the fragment and revision with a long uncemented stem
Open reduction with plate and cables without stem revision
items.e: Vancouver Type B1 – fracture around a well‑fixed stem; treatment is ORIF with plates and cables.

items.q: The ‘L’ in 316L stainless steel used for orthopedic implants denotes:
items.e: 316L refers to low carbon content, reducing notch sensitivity.

items.q: Which metal combination is MOST prone to galvanic corrosion in the joint space?
items.e: Titanium alloy in contact with cobalt–chromium forms the most severe galvanic couple.

items.q: During a direct lateral (Hardinge) approach, a split of gluteus medius more than 1 cm above the tip of the greater trochanter most endangers which nerve?
items.e: The superior gluteal nerve runs near the gluteus medius insertion and can be injured if the split is high.

items.q: What is the threshold joint reaction force across the hip in single‑leg stance?
items.e: Typical joint load is 2.5–3 times body weight in single‑leg stance.

items.q: The most common reason for proximal femoral fractures in revision THA with a long femoral stem is:
o: Proximal loss of support with a well‑fixed distal stem (cantilever bending)
items.e: Stem failure in revision is often due to cantilever bending of a well‑fixed distal stem.

items.q: Which shoulder or ankle implant surface coating aims for a porous thickness of 50–75 µm to promote osseointegration?
items.e: Hydroxyapatite coatings are optimally 50–75 µm for bone ongrowth.

items.q: The ‘effective joint space’ concept explains:
o: Wear particle dissemination via synovial fluid
items.e: It describes how wear particles travel distant from their origin through joint fluid.

items.q: In a total knee arthroplasty, increasing tibiofemoral conformity:
o: Decreases contact stress but increases fixation interface stress
items.e: Higher conformity reduces load per area but transfers more stress to fixation surfaces.

items.q: Which of the following is a major diagnostic criterion for periprosthetic joint infection according to the 2018 MSIS/ICM criteria?
o: Presence of a sinus tract communicating with the prosthesis
items.e: A sinus tract is one of the two major criteria for PJI.

items.q: The 80° cup inclination and 20° anteversion Lewinnek "safe zone" for acetabular components is:
items.e: Lewinnek’s safe zone is 55±5° inclination and 25±5° anteversion.

items.q: A ceramic head placed on a mildly damaged trunnion is best used with:
o: A ceramic head with a titanium adapter sleeve
items.e: Use a ceramic head with a titanium sleeve to avoid sharpening wear on a damaged trunnion.

items.q: Which statement about highly cross‑linked polyethylene (HXLPE) is FALSE?
o: It is produced by gamma irradiation in nitrogen
Free radicals generated during irradiation are scavenged by vitamin E
Remelting eliminates free radicals but reduces fatigue strength
It is cross‑linked by electron beam alone
items.e: Remelting does not eliminate free radicals; it reduces fatigue strength and toughness.

items.q: Two‑spot chondrosarcoma in the distal femur is most commonly classified under which objective tissue type?
items.e: Chondrosarcomas arise from cartilaginous tissue.

items.q: A patient with a long lumbar fusion has higher THA dislocation risk mainly because:
o: The pelvis cannot tilt posteriorly on sitting, reducing functional cup anteversion
items.e: Fixed pelvis limits posterior tilt, decreasing functional cup anteversion and raising dislocation risk.

items.q: Which of the following describes the failure mode of backside wear between a polyethylene liner and the metal acetabular shell?
items.e: Backside wear corresponds to Mode 4 wear.

items.q: A 68‑year‑old female presents with chronic groin pain and a prominent anterior acetabular rim on her post‑operative X‑ray. She had a primary total hip arthroplasty 10 years ago. Which of the following is the most likely cause of her symptoms?
items.e: A prominent anterior cup edge leads to iliopsoas impingement, a frequent cause of groin pain after THA.

items.q: During templating for a revision of a femoral stem with a well‑fixed distal tip, the surgeon plans a distal‑seam‑cutoplasty. For such a stem, which property of the cement mantle is most critical?
o: No cement washout at the tip
items.e: Cement mantle thickness of 4–6 mm is the accepted optimum; a thinner mantle leads to higher risk of stem pull‑out.

items.q: A 55‑year‑old man with a planar fracture of the intertrochanteric region is managed with a short cephalomedullary nail. Which bone‑plugged design advantage is unique to such nails?
items.e: The short head‑neck shaft plug enhances rotational stability of intertrochanteric fractures fixed with short nails.

items.q: Which of the following statements about highly cross‑linked polyethylene (HXLPE) is correct?
o: It has a higher modulus than conventional PE
It is more oxidised after remelting
Free radicals are scavenged by Vitamin E
It is produced by heat treatment only
items.e: Vitamin E is added to HXLPE to scavenge free radicals and reduce oxidation without compromising cross‑link density.

items.q: All of the following are true regarding the ‘epiphyseal marker’ in paediatric arthroplasty except:
o: It is used in hips with developmental dysplasia of the hip
It is a fixed cortical ridge
It is located at the acetabulum
It cannot be used after growth arrest
items.e: The epiphyseal marker is a cortical ridge within the femoral neck, not at the acetabulum.

items.q: Which of the following is NOT a recognised mode of third‑body wear in joint arthroplasty?
o: Bone fragments trapped at the cartilage/metal interface
items.e: Third‑body wear originates from bone, osteophytes or particulate debris, not from surgical gloves.

items.q: A 62‑year‑old woman develops unexplained swelling around the hip and elevated ESR after a primary THA. The surgeon suspects a prosthetic joint infection. Which investigation is most definitive for this diagnosis?
items.e: Joint aspiration with culture is the gold standard for diagnosing periprosthetic joint infection.

items.q: The most common normal‑world metal sensitiser among orthopaedic implant patients is:
items.e: Nickel is the most common metal sensitiser in the general population, including orthopaedic patients.

items.q: In the case of a patient with a long lumbar fusion, the risk of dislocation after a primary THA is primarily due to:
o: Insufficient functional cup anteversion from limited pelvic tilt
items.e: A fused lumbar spine limits posterior pelvic tilt, reducing functional cup anteversion and increasing dislocation risk.

items.q: Which of the following is the main biomechanical disadvantage of a rotating‑hinge knee prosthesis compared to a CCK insert in revision TKA?
o: Increased lever‑arm shear forces to the bone‑implant interface
Higher incidence of patellar tendon rupture
items.e: Rotating‑hinge implants transfer excess shear stresses across the bone–implant interface, increasing loosening risk.

items.q: A 73‑year‑old man with a revised total knee arthroplasty receives a polyethylene insert with a 6 mm thickness. This thickness is:
o: Excessive with risk of implant failure
The exact optimal thickness for all knees
items.e: The minimum recommended tibial polyethylene thickness in TKA is about 6 mm.

items.q: The system of Wasielewski acetabular quadrants is used to identify screws that may injure:
items.e: Screws in the anterosuperior quadrant of the acetabulum are close to the obturator nerve and vessels.

items.q: A 70-year-old woman falls from standing height. CT shows an L5 fracture involving the superior endplate with 35% loss of anterior height and a retropulsed fragment of the posterior wall; the inferior endplate is intact, the posterior tension band is intact and alignment is normal. How is this classified in the AO Spine thoracolumbar system?
o: A1 – wedge-compression (single endplate, no posterior wall involvement)
A3 – incomplete burst (one endplate plus posterior wall)
A4 – complete burst (both endplates plus posterior wall)
items.e: Posterior wall involvement with only one endplate fractured and an intact tension band is an AO A3 incomplete burst; A1 spares the posterior wall, A4 involves both endplates and B-types require tension band failure.

items.q: A 30‑year‑old construction worker presents with progressive thoracic back pain for 6 weeks. MRI shows a bony fragment eroding the posterior elements of T8 and an associated epidural hematoma causing mild spinal cord compression. What is the most urgent investigative step?
o: Immediate CT angiography of the aneurysm
CT of the thoracolumbar spine with 3‑D reconstruction
items.e: The magnetic resonance sequence reveals a bony fragment compressing the cord with an epidural hematoma. Rapid surgical decompression is indicated to prevent permanent neurological deficit.

items.q: A 12-year-old child falls from a 2-metre height and sustains a T10 burst fracture. Radiographs show loss of anterior and posterior vertebral body height with no translation, and the neurological examination is normal. According to the Denis three-column model, which column is most likely intact?
items.e: A Denis burst fracture is failure of the anterior and middle columns under axial load (retropulsion of the posterior body wall); in a stable burst fracture the posterior column (pedicles, facets, posterior ligamentous complex) remains intact. Failure of the middle column is what distinguishes a burst from a simple compression fracture.

items.q: The risk of neurological compromise in a thoracolumbar burst fracture can be best predicted by which radiographic parameter?
o: Degree of canal encroachment >50 % of the sagittal diameter
items.e: Severe canal encroachment (>50 % of the sagittal diameter) correlates strongly with spinal cord injury risk, whereas height loss, facet displacement, and kyphosis alone are less predictive.

items.q: A 45-year-old man is neurologically intact after a motorcycle crash. CT shows an L1 burst fracture; MRI shows high T2 signal in the interspinous ligament without a clear tear (PLC injury indeterminate). What is his TLICS score?
items.e: TLICS = morphology (burst 2) + neurology (intact 0) + PLC (indeterminate 2) = 4; a score of 4 is the grey zone where either operative or non-operative care is acceptable (≤3 non-operative, ≥5 operative).

items.q: During a staged fixation of a thoracolumbar fracture–dislocation, which intra‑operative adjunct is most reliable for confirming the quality of the pedicle screw purchase?
o: Pin pull testing with a calibrated force gauge
items.e: Pin pull testing with a calibrated gauge directly measures screw‑bone pullout strength, offering real‑time confirmation of purchase.

items.q: In a pediatric patient with a T12–L1 burst fracture, the appropriate revision strategy after an initial rigid halo vest immobilization that resulted in persistent pain is:
o: Exchange the halo for an external fixator
Add a posterior pedicle screw construct
Revise the halo with additional head pins
items.e: The most effective approach is to add a posterior pedicle screw construct to stabilize the fracture, especially when pain persists with external fixation alone.

items.q: A 28‑year‑old male sustains a high‑velocity motorcycle crash and develops sudden back pain. Plain radiographs show a burst fracture of T12 with a comminuted posterior wall fragment. Which of the following statements is most accurate regarding the management of this fracture?
o: Posterior pedicle screw fixation alone provides adequate stability because the posterior elements bear most of the load
An anterior corpectomy with titanium cage and plating is mandatory to restore height and anterior column support
Minimally invasive percutaneous pedicle screw fixation with bed rest for 12 weeks is sufficient
Combined anterior‑posterior instrumentation is preferable if kyphosis exceeds 30°
items.e: In a burst fracture with >30° kyphosis, combined anterior‑posterior fixation best restores alignment and prevents progressive deformity.

items.q: A 52‑year‑old woman falls onto a rolled mattress and presents with lower limb weakness and urinary incontinence. MRI shows a subarachnoid hematoma at L1‑L2 with a 10‑mm epidural bony fragment compressing the spinal cord. According to the Thoracolumbar Injury Classification and Severity Score (TLICS), what is the most appropriate treatment?
o: Anterior decompression with corpectomy and fusion
Posterior pedicle screw fixation with decompression and fusion
