cmvvzbs4efb7tv.e: [Lengthening the deltoid moment arm & recruiting deltoid fibers] RTSA shifts the center of rotation medially and inferiorly relative to the native glenohumeral joint. This increases the moment arm of the deltoid muscle and pre-tensions its fibers, enabling functional arm elevation in the presence of a deficient rotator cuff.

cmvvzbs4m8hunb.q: During revision TKA for a severe distal femoral bone defect involving the epicondyles (AORI Type III defect), which component constraint selection is required to provide joint stability?
o: Posterior Stabilized (PS) insert with long intramedullary stem
Cruciate Retaining (CR) design with offset stem
cmvvzbs4m8hunb.e: [Hinged (Rotating Hinge) Prosthesis] Epicondylar bone loss removes collateral ligament attachments (MCL/LCL). When collateral ligament integrity or peri-articular bone stock is completely compromised (AORI Type III), constrained or rotating- hinge implants are required to prevent gross coronal and sagittal instability. High-Yield Exam Pearl: Anderson Orthopaedic Research Institute (AORI) TKA Defect Classification • Type I (Minor): Intact metaphyseal bone; joint line unchanged; can be treated with standard augments or cement. • Type II (Metaphyseal): Damaged metaphyseal bone requiring modular augments, blocks, or sleeves/cones (2A: single condyle; 2B: both condyles). • Type III (Deficient Metaphysis/Collaterals): Massive bone loss involving epicondyles/collaterals; requires structural allograft, porous metal cones, and constrained hinged implants. Section E: Advanced THA Complications & Biomechanical Failures

cmvvzbs4rmhe0s.q: A 65-year-old male presents with deep groin pain 5 years after a bilateral Metal-on-Metal (MoM) THA. MRI reveals a solid pseudotumor surrounding the acetabulum without osseous destruction. Synovial fluid aspiration shows elevated Cobalt (18 ppb) and Chromium (14 ppb) levels. What is the characteristic histological finding of Adverse Local Tissue Reaction (ALTR / ALAVAL) in this patient?
o: Abundant foreign-body giant cells filled with polyethylene wear debris
Perivascular lymphocytic in filtrates (ALAVAL pattern) with tissue necrosis
Acute neutrophilic infiltration with fibrinopurulent exudate
Granulomatous inflammation with Langhans giant cells and caseation
cmvvzbs4rmhe0s.aText: Perivascular lymphocytic in filtrates (ALAVAL pattern) with tissue necrosis
cmvvzbs4rmhe0s.e: [Perivascular lymphocytic in filtrates (ALAVAL pattern) with tissue necrosis] Aseptic Lymphocyte-dominated Vasculitis-Associated Lesions (ALAVAL) are the classic histological hallmark of ALTR/pseudotumors caused by metal-on-metal wear or severe trunnionosis. Histology shows perivascular T- and B-lymphocytic aggregation, macrophage infiltration laden with metallic wear particles, and extensive soft tissue necrosis.

cmvvzbs4yyd7yc.q: In Paprosky classification of acetabular bone loss during revision THA, Type III-B defects are characterized by which specific radiographic and anatomical parameters?
o: Superior ischial lysis < 1 cm, teardrop intact, minimal superior migration
Severe Kohler's line break, superior migration > 3 cm, ischial lysis > 2 cm, high risk of pelvic discontinuity
Moderate Kohler's line disruption, superior migration 1 – 3 cm, intact teardrop
Intact acetabular rim with central cavitary defect only
cmvvzbs4yyd7yc.aText: Severe Kohler's line break, superior migration > 3 cm, ischial lysis > 2 cm, high risk of pelvic discontinuity
cmvvzbs4yyd7yc.e: [Severe Kohler's line break, superior migration > 3 cm, ischial lysis > 2 cm, pelvic discontinuity] Paprosky III-B represents severe up-and-in acetabular destruction: superior migration > 3 cm, severe ischial osteolysis (> 2 cm below teardrop), complete destruction of Kohler's line (ilioischial line break), and involvement of > 60% of the acetabular ring/columns, frequently accompanied by pelvic discontinuity.

cmvvzbs54ykmri.q: In cementless THA, proximal femoral "Stress Shielding" (Grumbridge/Engh classification) occurs primarily due to which mechanical phenomenon?
o: Micromotion at the bone-prosthesis interface > 150 μm preventing osseointegration
Load transfer occurring predominantly distally in a diaphyseal-engaging stiff stem, leaving the calcar unloaded
Interfacial thermal necrosis from exothermic PMMA polymerization
Excessive head size leading to increased frictional torque on the trunnion
cmvvzbs54ykmri.aText: Load transfer occurring predominantly distally in a diaphyseal-engaging stiff stem, leaving the calcar unloaded
cmvvzbs54ykmri.e: [Load transfer occurring predominantly distally in a diaphyseal-engaging stem] Wolff's law states bone remodels in response to stress. When a stiff, fully hydroxyapatite-coated or porous-coated stem achieves rigid fixation distally in the diaphysis, the mechanical loads bypass the proximal metaphyseal bone/calcar. Unloaded bone undergoes proximal resorptive bone loss (stress shielding). Paprosky Acetabular Bone Loss Classification Summary Type Superior Migration Ischial Osteolysis Kohler's Line Surgical Reconstruction Strategy Type I None None Intact Standard hemispherical cementless cup Type II (A- C) Mild (< 2 cm) Mild / None Intact / Minimal Jumbo cup, particulate graft, or modular augments Type III-A Moderate (2 – 3 cm) Moderate (< 1.5 cm) Intact Trabecular metal augments + cup / structural graft Section F: Complex TKA Alignment & Kinematics

cmvvzbs5fqei8p.q: During TKA gap balancing, a knee is found to be properly balanced in extension but excessively TIGHT in flexion. Which surgical resection adjustment will selectively increase the flexion space without altering the extension space?
o: Increasing posterior femoral condylar resection (posterior cut) or reducing femoral component size
Recutting the distal femur with 2° of additional flexion
cmvvzbs5fqei8p.aText: Increasing posterior femoral condylar resection (posterior cut) or reducing femoral component size
cmvvzbs5fqei8p.e: [Increasing posterior femoral resection / downsizing femoral component] The flexion gap is created between the posterior femoral condyles and the proximal tibial cut. Increasing posterior femoral resection (or downsizing the femoral component without anterior notch creation) enlarges the flexion gap selectively without affecting extension. Distal femoral cuts affect ONLY the extension space.

cmvvzbs5l4c3mw.q: In Total Knee Arthroplasty, raising the joint line (joint line elevation > 5 mm) due to excessive distal femoral resection compensated by a thicker poly spacer leads to which clinical complication?
o: Patellar Baja, reduced quadriceps moment arm, and flexion tightness
cmvvzbs5l4c3mw.e: Over-resecting the distal femur and filling the extension gap with a thicker insert raises the joint line. The patella then sits low relative to the new joint line (pseudo-patella baja, with patellofemoral impingement), and the altered collateral ligament isometry causes mid-flexion instability. True patella baja (option B) comes from patellar tendon shortening, not joint-line elevation.

cmvvzbs5rptlbd.q: In the Paprosky Classification of Femoral Bone Defects during revision THA, a Type III-B defect is best described by which structural characteristic?
o: Intact metaphysis with minimal osteolysis providing complete proximal support
Metaphyseal bone loss with intact diaphysis offering > 4 cm of intact diaphyseal bone for stem scratch fit
Severe metaphyseal-diapseal bone loss with < 4 cm of intact diaphyseal bone, requiring modular tapered fluted titanium stems or impaction grafting
Complete loss of cortical integrity from the metaphysis to the distal femur, requiring an allograft-prosthesis composite or total femur replacement
cmvvzbs5rptlbd.aText: Severe metaphyseal-diapseal bone loss with < 4 cm of intact diaphyseal bone, requiring modular tapered fluted titanium stems or impaction grafting
cmvvzbs5rptlbd.e: [Severe loss with < 4 cm intact diaphysis] Paprosky Type III-B femoral defects feature extensive metaphyseal and proximal diaphyseal osteolysis where less than 4 cm of intact diaphyseal canal remains for distal fixation. Type III-A has > 4 cm of intact diaphysis. Type III-B defects typically require modular tapered fluted stems that achieve distal bypass fixation.

cmvvzbs5zeo8mv.q: During Femoral Impaction Bone Grafting (IBG) in revision total hip arthroplasty, which bone graft preparation yields optimal structural stability and mechanical interlocking?
o: Fine ground bone slurry (< 1 mm) without washed marrow lipids
Morselized cancellous bone chips sized 8 – 10 mm, thoroughly washed of fat and blood content, tightly impacted
Large cortical struts > 30 mm placed strictly inside the medullary canal without cancellous packing
Unwashed morselized graft mixed in a 1:1 ratio with liquid PMMA cement
cmvvzbs5zeo8mv.aText: Morselized cancellous bone chips sized 8 – 10 mm, thoroughly washed of fat and blood content, tightly impacted
cmvvzbs5zeo8mv.e: [Morselized cancellous chips 8 – 10 mm, washed of fat/blood] According to the Exeter protocol for IBG, optimal graft stability requires washing fat/lipids out of the cancellous chips and using a particle size of 8 – 10 mm. Washed graft increases the coefficient of friction and shear strength between particles when impacted, providing a stable bed for cemented stem fixation.

cmvvzbs64yregq.q: What is the primary function of a Femoral Sleeve or Cone in Revision Total Knee Arthroplasty when addressing AORI Type II or III metaphyseal bone loss?
o: To bypass the joint completely and transfer all load into the diaphysis via a long un-cemented stem
To achieve zone 2 (metaphyseal) axial and rotational fixation, converting shear forces to compressive loads
To serve purely as a spacer without providing structural mechanical support
To reinforce patellar tendon re-attachment at the tibial tubercle
cmvvzbs64yregq.aText: To achieve zone 2 (metaphyseal) axial and rotational fixation, converting shear forces to compressive loads
cmvvzbs64yregq.e: [Achieve zone 2 metaphyseal axial/rotational fixation] The Morgan-Jones zonal fixation concept divides revision knee stability into 3 zones: Zone 1 (Epiphysis), Zone 2 (Metaphysis), and Zone 3 (Diaphysis). Metaphyseal sleeves and porous titanium cones establish robust Zone 2 fixation, transferring structural loads to host metaphyseal bone and protecting joint line reconstruction. Paprosky Femoral Bone Defect Classification Type Metaphyseal Support Intact Diaphyseal Canal Recommended Revision Stem Strategy Type I Intact Normal Standard primary cementless or cemented stem Type II Damaged / Minimal Intact Extensively porous-coated stem or modular stem Type III-A Severely compromised > 4 cm intact Extensively porous-coated stem or tapered fluted stem Type III-B Severely compromised < 4 cm intact Modular tapered fluted stem / Distal fixation stem Section H: Periprosthetic Joint Infection (PJI) Protocols & Robotics

cmvvzbs6bsmywp.q: A 72-year-old male with a history of right TKA performed 8 weeks ago presents with a acute 4-day history of severe knee pain, joint effusion, and fever. Synovial fluid aspiration yields 65,000 WBC/μL with 92% neutrophils. The implant is well- fixed without component loosening. What is the standard operative treatment strategy?
o: Single-stage exchange arthroplasty with antibiotic PMMA cement
Debridement, Antibiotic Retention, and Implant Exchange (DAIR) with modular liner exchange
Two-stage exchange arthroplasty with placement of an articulating spacer
Long-term suppressive oral antibiotic therapy without surgical intervention
cmvvzbs6bsmywp.aText: Debridement, Antibiotic Retention, and Implant Exchange (DAIR) with modular liner exchange
cmvvzbs6bsmywp.e: [DAIR with modular liner exchange] DAIR is indicated for acute PJI (symptoms < 3 weeks OR occurring within 4 weeks of index surgery) with well- fixed components, mature soft-tissue envelope, and absence of sinus tract. Modular liner exchange allows access to the posterior capsule for thorough synovectomy and decontamination of hidden bacterial bio films.

cmvvzbs6jfvoes.q: In two-stage revision arthroplasty for chronic Periprosthetic Joint Infection, what is the key advantage of an ARTICULATING antibiotic spacer over a STATIC spacer?
o: Significantly higher local elution rate of aminoglycosides and vancomycin
Maintenance of soft-tissue envelope length, preservation of ROM, and easier re-exposure during stage 2
Complete elimination of mechanical shear stress across host bone interfaces
Elimination of systemic toxicity from antibiotic PMMA leaching
cmvvzbs6jfvoes.aText: Maintenance of soft-tissue envelope length, preservation of ROM, and easier re-exposure during stage 2
cmvvzbs6jfvoes.e: [Maintenance of soft-tissue envelope length & easier re-exposure] Articulating antibiotic spacers maintain joint space height, preserve collateral ligament tension, reduce quadriceps shortening/arthrofibrosis, and improve functional mobility between stages. This significantly facilitates surgical exposure and dissection during the second-stage reimplantation.

cmvvzbs6o1cbim.q: In Image-Free (Haptic / Inertial) Robotic-Assisted Total Knee Arthroplasty, how does the system register bone landmarks and establish virtual surgical registration intraoperatively?
o: Preoperative 3D CT scan matched to intraoperative fluoroscopic projections
Optical tracker arrays attached to femur and tibia combined with anatomical point-probe mapping
Intraoperative ultrasound transducer arrays placed along the joint capsule
Preoperative full-leg standing digital X-ray calibrated with a radiopaque sphere
cmvvzbs6o1cbim.aText: Optical tracker arrays attached to femur and tibia combined with anatomical point-probe mapping
cmvvzbs6o1cbim.e: [Optical tracker arrays + point-probe anatomical mapping] Image-free robotic systems utilize rigid body arrays with infrared optical spheres attached to the femur and tibia. The surgeon uses a tracked digitizing probe to paint the articular surfaces and register specific anatomical landmarks (center of femoral head, epicondyles, tibial center), creating a real-time kinematic profile without requiring a preoperative CT scan. High-Yield Exam Pearl: Zonal Fixation in Revision Arthroplasty (Morgan-Jones Concept) • Zone 1 (Epiphyseal/Joint Surface): Reconstructed with augments, offset adapters, or impaction graft. • Zone 2 (Metaphyseal): Primary area for load transfer using porous metal cones or titanium sleeves. • Zone 3 (Diaphyseal): Provides rotational alignment and alignment stability via cementlessfluted stems or cemented smooth stems. Successful revision requires solid engagement in at least TWO of the three zones. INI-SS SUPER-SPECIALTY EXAMINATION Arthroplasty & Joint Reconstructive Surgery Module 1: Memory-Based Previous Year MCQs, High-Yield Concepts & Analytical Explanations Section A: Total Hip Arthroplasty (THA) Biomechanics & Surgery

cmvvzbs6tv4l4y.q: During an Anterior Approach (Hueter) to the hip joint, bleeding is encountered in the intermuscular plane between the Tensor Fasciae Latae (TFL) and Sartorius. Which vessel is most vulnerable to injury at this stage?
o: Ascending Branch of Lateral Femoral Circumflex Artery (LFCA)
First Perforating Artery of Profunda Femoris
cmvvzbs6tv4l4y.aText: Ascending Branch of Lateral Femoral Circumflex Artery (LFCA)
cmvvzbs6tv4l4y.e: [Ascending Branch of LFCA] The internervous plane for the direct anterior approach is between the TFL (Superior Gluteal N.) and Sartorius (Femoral N.). Deep in this interval, the ascending branch of the lateral femoral circumflex artery crosses horizontally and must be identified, ligated, or cauterized to prevent brisk arterial bleeding and postoperative hematoma formation.

cmvvzbs71s22my.q: During a primary TKA, after completing distal femoral and proximal tibial resections, you assess the joint gaps with a spacer block. The gap is found to be tight in extension, but perfectly balanced in flexion. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step?
cmvvzbs71s22my.e: Resect additional distal femur. Distal femoral resection directly impacts ONLY the extension gap without altering the flexion gap. Resecting additional proximal tibia increases both flexion and extension gaps. Releasing the posterior capsule is reserved for fixed flexion deformities when bone cuts are completed.

cmvvzbs7658ukv.q: In a TKA for a severe fixed valgus deformity (>15 degrees), which of the following sequences of lateral soft tissue releases is considered standard practice?
cmvvzbs7658ukv.e: Osteophytes → ITB subperiosteal → Popliteus / LCL. Removal of osteophytes is always the FIRST step in soft-tissue balancing. For valgus knees: ITB release corrects tightness mainly in extension; Popliteus release corrects tightness mainly in flexion; LCL release corrects tightness in both. Over-release of LCL/Popliteus necessitates a constrained liner.

cmvvzbs7bvr9qx.q: A patient undergoing TKA has a pre-operative fixed flexion deformity (FFD) of 25°. Which step is essential during femoral component positioning to avoid flexion-gap tightness?
o: Downsize the femoral component and shift anteriorly
Upsize the femoral component with posterior augmentation
Ensure adequate posterior femoral condylar resection and posterior capsular release
cmvvzbs7bvr9qx.aText: Ensure adequate posterior femoral condylar resection and posterior capsular release
cmvvzbs7bvr9qx.e: Ensure adequate posterior femoral condylar resection and posterior capsular release. FFD requires bone resections that restore extension space (e.g., additional distal femur cut, posterior osteophyte resection, posterior capsular strip, and release of gastrocnemius heads). Under-resecting posterior condyles compromises flexion space and produces flexion tightness. High-Yield Rule for TKA Gap Balancing: Tight in Extension & Flexion: Resect more proximal tibia or use thinner tibial insert. Tight in Extension ONLY: Resect more distal femur or release posterior capsule. Tight in Flexion ONLY: Recess posterior cruciate ligament (PCL), increase posterior femoral slope, or downsize femoral component. TOTAL HIP ARTHROPLASTY (THA): BIOMECHANICS, ORIENTATIONS & TRIBOLOGY

cmvvzbs7lvykgp.q: What are the classical Lewinnek safe zones for acetabular cup orientation in primary Total Hip Arthroplasty?
cmvvzbs7lvykgp.e: Inclination: 40° ± 10° (30° – 50°), Anteversion: 15° ± 10° (5° – 25°). Standard safe zones established by Lewinnek minimize posterior dislocation and edge loading. Current functional positioning concepts also account for spinomedicular pelvic tilt (pelvic tilt increases by ~1° for every 1° of lumbar flexion).

cmvvzbs7q31wo9.q: According to Wasielewski's quadrant system for acetabular cup screw fixation, which quadrant is designated as the SAFE zone to avoid vascular and neurological injury?
cmvvzbs7q31wo9.e: Posterosuperior quadrant. A line from the anterior superior iliac spine (ASIS) through the center of the acetabulum divides it into anterior and posterior halves. The Posterosuperior quadrant allows secure screw purchase into thick iliac bone without risking external iliac vessels (anterosuperior) or obturator vessels/nerve (anteroinferior).

cmvvzbs7vllg6m.q: In ceramic-on-ceramic (CoC) bearing surfaces in total hip arthroplasty, "squeaking" is most closely linked to which mechanical phenomenon?
o: Edge loading and loss of fluid- film lubrication
Oxidation of ultra-high molecular weight polyethylene
cmvvzbs7vllg6m.aText: Edge loading and loss of fluid- film lubrication
cmvvzbs7vllg6m.e: Edge loading and loss of fluid- film lubrication. Ceramic bearings rely on fluid- film lubrication. Micro-separation, cup steepness (>50° inclination), or impingement breaks this fluid film, causing stripe wear and high-frequency acoustical vibration ("squeaking"). Volumetric wear in CoC is extremely low (<1 mm³/year). ANATOMY & QUADRANT SAFETY IN ACETABULAR FIXATION Quadrant Key Anatomical Structures at Risk Safety Classification Posterosuperior Thick sciatic buttress bone (Sciatic nerve distance >20mm) SAFE ZONE (Primary screw target) Posteroinferior Inferior gluteal vessels, Internal pudendal vessels, Sciatic nerve CAUTION ZONE (Short screws only <20mm) Anterosuperior External iliac artery and vein DANGER ZONE (High risk of bleeding) Anteroinferior Obturator artery, vein, and obturator nerve DANGER ZONE (Avoid screws entirely) COMPLICATIONS: PERIPROSTHETIC JOINT INFECTION (PJI) & FRACTURES

cmvvzbs82qzhga.q: According to the 2018 Musculoskeletal Infection Society (MSIS) / International Consensus Meeting (ICM) criteria, which of the following constitutes a MAJOR diagnostic criterion for Periprosthetic Joint Infection (PJI)?
o: Presence of a sinus tract communicating with the prosthesis
cmvvzbs82qzhga.aText: Presence of a sinus tract communicating with the prosthesis
cmvvzbs82qzhga.e: Presence of a sinus tract communicating with the prosthesis. MSIS/ICM criteria define 2 MAJOR criteria (either is diagnostic of PJI): 1) Sinus tract communicating with the joint; OR 2) Two positive identical pre-operative or intra-operative cultures. Serum CRP, synovial WBC, and alpha-defensin form minor scoring criteria.

cmvvzbs882xhjm.q: A 72-year-old female presents 4 years post-primary cementless THA following a fall. Radiographs show a fracture around the tip of a well- fixed femoral stem with moderate bone stock degradation. According to the Vancouver classification, how is this fracture categorized and managed?
o: Vancouver Type B1; Revision with long uncemented stem
Vancouver Type B1; Open reduction and internal fixation (ORIF) with plate & cables
Vancouver Type B2; ORIF with locking plate alone
cmvvzbs882xhjm.aText: Vancouver Type B1; Open reduction and internal fixation (ORIF) with plate & cables
cmvvzbs882xhjm.e: Vancouver Type B1; ORIF with plate & cables. Vancouver Type B1 fractures occur around or just distal to the stem with a WELL-FIXED stem . Treatment is ORIF with locked plating and strut allografts/cables. Type B2 (loose stem, good bone) requires revision arthroplasty with a long stem. Type B3 (loose stem, poor bone) requires revision with fluted tapered stem or proximal femoral replacement.

cmvvzbs8d2ap13.q: Which organism is most commonly associated with early acute PJI (<4 weeks post-op) and is known for biofilm formation that makes DAIR (Debridement, Antibiotics, and Implant Retention) challenging without specific anti-biofilm agents?
cmvvzbs8d2ap13.e: Staphylococcus aureus / Staphylococcus epidermidis. Staphylococci produce exopolysaccharide slime layer bio films on metal/polyethylene implants. Rifampicin is added to antimicrobial regimens specifically for its ability to penetrate Staphylococcal bio films during DAIR procedures. Summary: Vancouver Classification of Periprosthetic Femoral Fractures Type A: Trochanteric region (AG = Greater Trochanter, AL = Lesser Trochanter). Rx: Conservative or tension-band. Type B1: Around/distal to stem; Stem WELL-FIXED . Rx: ORIF (Plate + Cables ± Strut). Type B2: Around/distal to stem; Stem LOOSE , bone adequate. Rx: Revision to long uncemented stem. Type B3: Around/distal to stem; Stem LOOSE , poor bone stock. Rx: Revision stem / Proximal Femoral Replacement. Type C: Well distal to stem tip. Rx: ORIF independently of prosthesis. INI-SS MCh Arthroplasty 25 High-Yield Recall MCQs COMPLEX REVISION, PERIPROSTHETIC FRACTURES, INFECTION & TRIBOLOGY Target: INI-SS / NEET-SS / AIIMS MCh Arthroplasty 25 High-Yield Boards Recall Questions High-Yield Core Review SECTION 1: COMPLEX REVISION KNEE & BIOMECHANICS (Q1 – Q5)

cmvvzbs8jwhq8j.q: In revision TKA with massive uncontained metaphyseal bone defects (AORI Type III), which reconstructive modality provides the highest rate of biological osseointegration and structural fixation?
o: Highly porous titanium / Tantalum metaphyseal sleeves or cones
cmvvzbs8jwhq8j.aText: Highly porous titanium / Tantalum metaphyseal sleeves or cones
cmvvzbs8jwhq8j.e: Highly porous titanium / Tantalum metaphyseal sleeves or cones. Porous tantalum/titanium cones and sleeves achieve zonal fixation in Zone 2 (metaphysis), bypassing damaged Zone 1 (epiphysis). Structural allografts carry risks of late collapse and non-union, whereas cement alone exhibits high failure rates in large uncontained defects.

cmvvzbs8qy7frc.q: A patient with severe recurvatum deformity (>15°) undergoes revision TKA. To correct the recurvatum and prevent hyperextension instability, which strategy is most appropriate?
o: Resect additional distal femur and insert a thinner polyethylene
Proximalize the femoral component, augment distal femur, and increase posterior tibial slope
Distalize the joint line by augmenting the distal femur and using a thicker polyethylene insert
Release the posterior capsule and Gastrocnemius insertion
cmvvzbs8qy7frc.aText: Distalize the joint line by augmenting the distal femur and using a thicker polyethylene insert
cmvvzbs8qy7frc.e: Distalize the joint line by augmenting the distal femur and using a thicker polyethylene insert. Hyperextension/recurvatum results from excessive extension space. Distalizing the femoral component (using distal femoral augments) and increasing poly thickness tightens the extension space and restores the joint line without compromising the flexion gap.

cmvvzbs8xl9ino.q: During revision TKA, an stem is added to the tibial component. According to engineering principles, what percentage of axial load is transmitted through a fully engaged offset/press- fit stem away from the metaphysis?
cmvvzbs8xl9ino.e: 30% – 50%. Diaphyseal stem engagement stress-shields the surrounding bone by transferring 30% to 50% of the axial load away from the proximal tibia into the diaphysis, protecting metaphyseal bone grafts or cones during healing.

cmvvzbs9b3msad.q: According to the Paprosky Classification of Acetabular Bone Loss in Revision THA, which type is characterized by total loss of the posterior column and superior migration >3 cm with pelvic discontinuity?
cmvvzbs9b3msad.e: Type IIIB. Paprosky Type IIIB involves severe acetabular rim destruction (>60%), loss of posterior column, teardrop osteolysis, and >3 cm superior hip center migration with high risk of pelvic discontinuity. Type IIIA has >3 cm migration but intact posterior column supporting cup stability.

cmvvzbs9gl4sk4.q: In managing a true pelvic discontinuity during revision THA with Paprosky Type IIIB defects, which structural construct offers the highest stability?
o: Jumbo acetabular cup with 2 trans- fixation screws
Cemented cup inside an impaction bone graft bed
Cup-cage construct or Custom triflange acetabular component (CTAC)
Standalone porous tantalum augment without posterior column plating
cmvvzbs9gl4sk4.aText: Cup-cage construct or Custom triflange acetabular component (CTAC)
cmvvzbs9gl4sk4.e: Cup-cage construct or Custom triflange acetabular component (CTAC). Pelvic discontinuity separates upper and lower pelvis. Fixation requires bridging the defect onto ilium and ischium using a cup-cage construct, custom 3D printed triflange implant, or distraction with modular tantalum cages.

cmvvzbs9nnu28i.q: During revision THA, a extended trochanteric osteotomy (ETO) is performed to remove a firmly fixed stem. What is the maximum recommended length of an ETO measured from the tip of the greater trochanter?
cmvvzbs9nnu28i.e: 12 – 15 cm. An ETO should provide exposure while preserving at least 5 to 7 cm of intact distal diaphyseal bone for press- fit fixation of the revision fluted tapered stem. It is typically 12 – 15 cm measured from the tip of the greater trochanter.

cmvvzbs9u9xno5.q: Which modular femoral revision stem design demonstrates the lowest rate of subsidence in Paprosky Type IIIB femoral bone defects?
o: Splined, fluted, tapered titanium stem (Conical taper 2° to 3°)
cmvvzbs9u9xno5.aText: Splined, fluted, tapered titanium stem (Conical taper 2° to 3°)
cmvvzbs9u9xno5.e: Splined, fluted, tapered titanium stem (Conical taper 2° to 3°). Modular fluted tapered stems rely on splines to engage diaphyseal bone and provide rotational stability, while the taper provides vertical wedge stability. They achieve superior scratch fit in deficient diaphyses compared to cylindrical stems.

cmvvzbsa0xho26.q: Dual-mobility acetabular constructs significantly reduce dislocation rates in revision THA. What is the primary mechanism of dual-mobility bearings?
o: Increasing the offset of the abductor muscle mechanism by 15 mm
Increasing the effective head size and jump distance while retaining a small inner femoral head diameter
Completely locking the liner inside the metal shell
cmvvzbsa0xho26.aText: Increasing the effective head size and jump distance while retaining a small inner femoral head diameter
cmvvzbsa0xho26.e: Increasing the effective head size and jump distance. Dual mobility features two articulation points: inner head inside a large poly liner, and outer poly liner inside the smooth shell. This offers a large jump distance (distance the femoral head must travel to dislocate) while maintaining low volumetric wear. SECTION 3: PERIPROSTHETIC FRACTURES & FIXATION STRATEGIES (Q11 – Q15)

cmvvzbsa9gbyni.q: A 68-year-old male presents with a periprosthetic knee fracture involving the distal femur around a well- fixed PS femoral component (Supracondylar Felix/Lewis Type II). Which construct is the gold standard treatment?
o: Immediate revision to a distal femoral replacement (DFR)
Retrograde intramedullary nail or distal femoral lateral locking compression plate (LCP)
Long leg cast immobilization for 8 weeks
Tension band wiring with cerclage cables
cmvvzbsa9gbyni.aText: Retrograde intramedullary nail or distal femoral lateral locking compression plate (LCP)
cmvvzbsa9gbyni.e: Retrograde intramedullary nail or distal femoral lateral locking compression plate (LCP). If the prosthesis is stable/well- fixed, fixation with a locked plate or retrograde nail (if the box of the PS component allows passage) is indicated. Revision to DFR is reserved for loose implants or severe comminuted non-reconstructable bone loss.

cmvvzbsaeksvyg.q: According to the UCS (Unified Classification System) for periprosthetic fractures, how is a fracture occurring in a bone containing an implant, but NOT surrounding the implant (e.g., intertrochanteric fracture above an ipsilateral TKA stem), classified?
cmvvzbsaeksvyg.e: Class C. In the Unified Classification System (Duncan and Haddad), type C is a fracture clear of the implant in a bone that contains one, such as a fracture well away from a TKA femoral component. B is around or next to an implant (B1 well fixed, B2 loose, B3 poor bone), D divides a bone between two implants, E involves each of two bones supporting one arthroplasty, F is an unreplaced joint surface articulating with an implant (e.g. the acetabulum opposite a hemiarthroplasty), and A is apophyseal or extra-articular (e.g. greater trochanter).

cmvvzbsajy1v6j.q: In periprosthetic acetabular fractures associated with THA, which factor is the single most critical determinant in deciding between ORIF and revision arthroplasty?
o: Stability/ fixation status of the acetabular cup
Use of cemented vs. uncemented cup
cmvvzbsajy1v6j.aText: Stability/ fixation status of the acetabular cup
cmvvzbsajy1v6j.e: Stability/ fixation status of the acetabular cup. Like femoral periprosthetic fractures, cup stability dictates management. If the cup is stable (Della Valle Type I/II), non- operative or ORIF is chosen. If loose (Della Valle Type III/IV), revision of the acetabular shell is required.

cmvvzbsaoswtxr.q: Intraoperative fracture of the medial malleolus during TKA is best managed intraoperatively by which technique?
o: Tension band wiring or partially threaded cannulated cancellous screw fixation
Revision to a constrained hinge knee
cmvvzbsaoswtxr.aText: Tension band wiring or partially threaded cannulated cancellous screw fixation
cmvvzbsaoswtxr.e: Tension band wiring or partially threaded cancellous screw fixation. Intraoperative fracture of the medial malleolus compromises the deltoid ligament attachment, causing severe acute ankle/tibial instability. Rigid internal fixation with CC screws or tension band wiring is required immediately.

cmvvzbsat6t153.q: A periprosthetic fracture occurs at the anterior notch of the distal femoral cortex created during primary TKA. What degree of anterior femoral cortical notching increases the risk of fracture by >40%?
o: Cortical notching does not alter fracture risk
cmvvzbsat6t153.e: Notch depth > 3 mm (or >25% cortical thickness). Anterior femoral cortical notching creates a local stress riser. Biomechanical studies confirm that notches >3 mm significantly reduce torsional strength of the distal femur by 29% to 40%. SECTION 4: PJI DIAGNOSTICS, ANTIBIOTIC SPACERS & MANAGEMENT (Q16 – Q20)

cmvvzbsb62w9pq.q: In the DAIR (Debridement, Antibiotics, and Implant Retention) procedure for acute PJI, which of the following steps is MANDATORY to maximize treatment success?
o: Retaining the original modular polyethylene insert to prevent joint instability
Exchange of all modular components (polyethylene insert, femoral head)
Performing the procedure only after 8 weeks of systemic oral antibiotics
cmvvzbsb62w9pq.aText: Exchange of all modular components (polyethylene insert, femoral head)
cmvvzbsb62w9pq.e: Exchange of all modular components (polyethylene insert, femoral head). Exchanging modular components allows access to the posterior capsule and underlying interfaces to clear biofilm buildup, significantly increasing DAIR success rate from <50% to >80%.

cmvvzbsbbzizfq.q: A synovial fluid biomarker test shows elevated Alpha-defensin. What is the sensitivity and specificity of the Alpha-defensin immunoassay in diagnosing PJI?
cmvvzbsbbzizfq.e: Sensitivity >95%, Specificity >95%. Alpha-defensin is an antimicrobial peptide released by neutrophils in response to pathogens. It is resistant to prior antibiotic therapy interference and maintains high accuracy (>95% sensitivity and specificity).

cmvvzbsbganknx.q: What is the ideal timing for obtaining pre-operative joint aspiration for culture in a patient suspected of PJI who is currently receiving oral antibiotic therapy?
o: Aspiration should be performed immediately without stopping antibiotics
Antibiotics should be withheld for at least 2 weeks prior to aspiration
Antibiotics should be stopped for 24 hours prior to aspiration
Aspiration is contraindicated if antibiotics were given within 6 months
cmvvzbsbganknx.aText: Antibiotics should be withheld for at least 2 weeks prior to aspiration
cmvvzbsbganknx.e: Antibiotics should be withheld for at least 2 weeks prior to aspiration. Active antibiotic therapy inhibits organism growth in culture media, causing false-negative synovial fluid cultures. A 2-week antibiotic-free window (drug holiday) is required before diagnostic joint aspiration.

cmvvzbsblm7py2.q: In two-stage revision arthroplasty for PJI, what is the minimum duration of targeted systemic antibiotic therapy recommended before considering re-implantation?
cmvvzbsblm7py2.e: 4 to 6 weeks. The standard international guideline specifies 4 – 6 weeks of targeted pathogen-specific antibiotic therapy (often IV initially, followed by high-bioavailability oral agents) prior to clinical re-evaluation for stage two re-implantation. SECTION 5: BIOMATERIALS, TRIBOLOGY & HIGH-YIELD CORE (Q21 – Q25)

cmvvzbsbvf9655.q: "Trunnionosis" in THA refers to mechanically assisted crevice corrosion (MACC) at which implant interface?
cmvvzbsbvf9655.e: Femoral head-stem taper interface (12/14 taper). Trunnionosis occurs at the head-neck taper junction due to micromotion, fretting, and fluid ingress, releasing Co and Cr ions that trigger adverse local tissue reactions (ALTR) or pseudotumors.

cmvvzbsce4gb5y.q: Which implant alloy has the elastic modulus closest to human cortical bone (~15 – 20 GPa), minimizing stress shielding?
cmvvzbsce4gb5y.e: Beta-Titanium alloys (~40 – 55 GPa). Standard Ti-6Al-4V has a modulus of ~110 GPa. Newer Beta-Titanium alloys reduce this to ~40 – 55 GPa, closer to cortical bone (15 – 20 GPa), significantly reducing distal stress shielding and proximal femoral thigh pain. cmvy0169fynytv.q: A 45-year-old man is neurologically intact after a motorcycle crash. CT shows an L1 burst fracture; MRI shows high T2 signal in the interspinous ligament without a clear tear (PLC injury indeterminate). What is his TLICS score?
cmvy0169fynytv.e: TLICS = morphology (burst 2) + neurology (intact 0) + PLC (indeterminate 2) = 4; a score of 4 is the grey zone where either operative or non-operative care is acceptable (≤3 non-operative, ≥5 operative).

cmvy0168tjebrj.q: A 12-year-old child falls from a 2-metre height and sustains a T10 burst fracture. Radiographs show loss of anterior and posterior vertebral body height with no translation, and the neurological examination is normal. According to the Denis three-column model, which column is most likely intact?
cmvy0168tjebrj.e: A Denis burst fracture is failure of the anterior and middle columns under axial load (retropulsion of the posterior body wall); in a stable burst fracture the posterior column (pedicles, facets, posterior ligamentous complex) remains intact. Failure of the middle column is what distinguishes a burst from a simple compression fracture.

cai20261109_028.q: A 66-year-old has a painful, swollen knee 3 weeks after primary TKA. According to the 2018 ICM definition, which synovial fluid thresholds suggest acute periprosthetic joint infection (within 6 weeks of surgery)?
cai20261109_028.e: Early postoperative haemarthrosis and inflammation raise synovial counts, so acute PJI thresholds are higher (WBC >10,000/µL, PMN >90%) than for chronic PJI (WBC >3,000/µL, PMN >80%). Serum CRP threshold is also higher early (about 100 mg/L).

cmvy01682fdtx4.q: A 70-year-old woman falls from standing height. CT shows an L5 fracture involving the superior endplate with 35% loss of anterior height and a retropulsed fragment of the posterior wall; the inferior endplate is intact, the posterior tension band is intact and alignment is normal. How is this classified in the AO Spine thoracolumbar system?
o: A1 – wedge-compression (single endplate, no posterior wall involvement)
A3 – incomplete burst (one endplate plus posterior wall)
A4 – complete burst (both endplates plus posterior wall)
cmvy01682fdtx4.aText: A3 – incomplete burst (one endplate plus posterior wall)
cmvy01682fdtx4.e: Posterior wall involvement with only one endplate fractured and an intact tension band is an AO A3 incomplete burst; A1 spares the posterior wall, A4 involves both endplates and B-types require tension band failure.

cai20261110_021.q: Which quantitative cartilage MRI technique uses delayed imaging after intravenous gadolinium to estimate the glycosaminoglycan content of articular cartilage, for example after cartilage repair?
cai20261110_021.e: Negatively charged gadolinium distributes inversely to the negatively charged GAGs, so dGEMRIC T1 maps reflect proteoglycan content; T2 mapping mainly reflects water content and collagen network organisation.

cai20261110_033.q: During wrist arthroscopy for suspected scapholunate ligament injury, the probe can be passed between the scaphoid and lunate from the midcarpal portal, but a 2.7 mm arthroscope cannot be passed through the interval. What is the Geissler grade?
cai20261110_033.e: Geissler: I – attenuation seen from radiocarpal side only; II – incongruency/step-off seen from midcarpal side; III – step-off with a gap admitting a probe; IV – gross instability with a 2.7 mm scope passing through the gap ('drive-through' sign).

cai20261110_034.q: A 40-year-old woman has polyostotic fibrous dysplasia of the femur and pelvis together with multiple intramuscular myxomas in the thigh. What is this association called?
cai20261110_034.e: Mazabraud syndrome is fibrous dysplasia (usually polyostotic) with intramuscular myxomas, both linked to activating GNAS mutations; McCune–Albright adds café-au-lait spots and endocrinopathy, and Maffucci is enchondromatosis with haemangiomas.
